💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bruno Fernandes missed a penalty for the second successive pre-season friendly as Manchester United were beaten 4-2 by former head coach Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan.
  • Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.
  • His effort was on target this time, but Milan keeper Lorenzo Torriani dived to his right to beat the shot away.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bruno Fernandes missed a penalty for the second successive pre-season friendly as Manchester United were beaten 4-2 by former head coach Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan.

Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.

His effort was on target this time, but Milan keeper Lorenzo Torriani dived to his right to beat the shot away.

Fernandes did at least get an assist, taking the second-minute corner which was powerfully headed home by Harry Maguire to give United the lead.

Amorim’s Milan equalised after a defensive mix-up allowed Gonçalo Ramos to break into the area and square for Samuel Chukwueze to roll home.

United were awarded their penalty just before half-time after Koni De Winter tugged back Youri Tielemans, but Torriani guessed correctly to leave Fernandes frustrated.

United retook the lead after Patrick Dorgu pounced on a loose backpass from Filippo Terracciano, but Milan equalised again when Chukwueze’s wayward shot was poked in by Alphadjo Cissè at the far post.

Marcus Rashford, who was frozen out by Amorim and loaned out to Aston Villa and then Barcelona, came on as a substitute on the hour for his first United appearance since returning from Spain.

But Milan went ahead in the 68th minute when Chukwueze’s cross was headed home by Ramos, and three minutes later former Chelsea midfielder Ruben Loftus-Cheek raced through to hit the fourth and cap a performance that underlines United’s need for reinforcements before their season starts in earnest next Saturday, away at Hull City.

Manchester United (4-2-3-1) Lammens; Mazraoui (Dalot 61), Maguire, Heaven (Martinez 61), Shaw; Tielemans, Santos (Mainoo 61); Diallo (Lacey 61), Fernandes, Dorgu (Rashford 61); Cunha (Mbeumo 61). Subs Zirkzee, Yoro, J Fletcher, T Fletcher, Amass, Collyer, Mee (g), Heath (g), Gabriel. Booked Dorgu.

Industry observers note that AC Milan (3-4-2-1) Torriani; Terracciano (Gila 60), Winter (Vladimirov 84), Pavlovic (Diawara 84); Chukwueze, Musah (Ricci 76), Jashari (Modric 60), Estupinan (Bartesaghi 61); Loftus-Cheek (Comotto 84), Cisse (Saelemaekers 60); Ramos (Camarda 75). Subs Pittarella (g), Bouyer (g). Booked Estupinan.

Goals Chukwueze (37), Cisse (57), Ramos (68), Loftus-Cheek (71).

United’s pre-season ends in defeat. A wretched second half proves their undoing as Amorim’s Milan score four. Worth reminding that United led this match, twice.

Milan are playing keep-ball in these latter stages and although Mainoo regains possession, his attempt to play forward is cut out and Modric’s outside-of-the-foot pass finds Comotto, who heads straight at Lammens.

Four minutes of added time to be played...

United now raining crosses down on Milan’s box but Torriani equal to it every time.

For the second time this afternoon, Shaw directs a lovely ball into Fernandes’ path in behind Milan’s back line, but the Portugal international can’t bring it under his spell.

Martinez has added a little bit of urgency to United’s build-up. Mbeumo tries to feed Shaw down the line but the ball is cut out.

More substitutions... Diawara, Vladimirov and Comotto enter the field of play in place of Pavlovic, De Winter and Loftus-Cheek.

Major chance for Rashford! Martinez lofts a fantastic ball over the top but Rashford is not quite able to bring it under his spell, with Torriani and De Winter combing to clear their lines.

Sources indicate that milan are now sitting off, settling into a back five as they look to preserve their advantage. Fernandes, Tielemans and Dalot combine well but such has been United’s fortunes this afternoon, the ball ricochets off the referee and play is halted.

Good work from Rashford in the corner to regain possession, but his ball into the box is not picked up by a team-mate.

Sources indicate that more changes... Ramos and Musah make way for Camarda and Ricci.

Sources indicate that manchester United 2 AC Milan 4 (Loftus-Cheek) No sooner had the players returned after the second-half hydration break then Milan exploit United’s exposed left side (again). Ramos sends Loftus-Cheek through and the midfielder composes himself before bending the ball around Lammens.

Manchester United 2 AC Milan 3 (Ramos) That’s too easy. United fail to learn their lesson, Shaw not getting tight enough to Chukwueze and the winger’s cross is met by new signing Ramos, who powers a header back across goal and past Lammens.

Loftus-Cheek and Ramos are doing a good job of cutting off the pass into United’s midfield in their build-up phase.

Wholesale changes on the hour mark...

Rashford (who makes his first United appearance in almost two years), Lacey, Dalot, Mbeumo, Mainoo and Martinez replace Dorgu, Amad, Mazraoui, Cunha, Santos and Heaven.

For Milan, Saelemaekers, Bartesaghi, Gila and Modric are on for Cisse, Estupinan, Terracciano and Jashari.

Manchester United 2 AC Milan 2 (Cisse) United have set a higher defensive line so far this half, with their front line pressing with more intensity to avoid the ball over the top. However Chukwueze is able to find space around the sides, coming in off the right and curling an effort goalwards which Cisse turns in at the far post. There are calls for offside, but with no VAR here, the goal stands.

In a recent development, milan win a free-kick some 25 yards out after Fernandes clips Estupinan. Teenager Cisse steps up and fires straight into the United wall. Was always going to be difficult to trouble Lammens from there.

According to recent reports, manchester United 2 AC Milan 1 (Dorgu) United wisely decide to keep hold of the ball for a while, the midfield three rotating to disrupt Milan’s out-of-possession shape and open up passing lanes. A Milan throw-in from the right-back berth is precedes an awful backpass by Terracciano which is pounced on by Dorgu who curls the ball beyond Torriani.

In a recent development, united have looked bright in the opening moments of this half. They win a free-kick midway into Milan’s half. The ball is delivered to the back post and, after some 18-yard-box pinball, a relieved Torriano pounces on it.

Both teams remain unchanged as the second 45 minutes begin.

In a recent development, all square at the break. Tough to know what to make of that half – United looked solid enough and could have taken a lead into the interval had Fernandes converted his penalty, but they failed to create a wealth of clear-cut chances. It will be interesting to see how Carrick approaches this second half.

Milan have enjoyed just a tick over two-thirds of possession, which United have contributed to in part through some lackadaisical passing.

Fernandes misses a spot-kick for the second time in two friendlies! Here, Torriani guesses correctly, diving to his right to palm Fernandes’ strike away.

De Winter brings down Tielemans inside the box after Terracciano loses the ball attempting to play out from the back.

Recent findings suggest that manchester United 1 AC Milan 1 (Chukwueze) It’s all a bit messy. Jashari causes Maguire and Santos to crash into each other (Kaka at Old Trafford, anyone?) off a throw-in, Ramos taking over with the United pair out of commission. He finds Chukwueze who finishes the move off at the far post.

The match becomes stretched momentarily as Pavlovic, the centre-back, marauds forward, setting the ball to Estupinan who delivers another dangerous cross from the left, which Lammens does well to claim.

Santos clips Loftus-Cheek near the byline and the referee awards Milan a free-kick. Chukwueze cuts the ball back to an unmarked Jashari on the edge of the box, but his side-footed effort flies wide.

Milan supporters unfurl a banner paying tribute to the late, great Franco Baresi, who passed away on July 31 aged 66.

United have picked their moments to press. Santos, who has enjoyed a wonderful pre-season, is a little too overzealous in his attempts to regain possession and gives away a foul. But the intent is correct.

In a recent development, shaw floats a delightful ball over the top for Fernandes to gallop on to. The Portuguese steals in ahead of De Winter but cannot find the target with his weaker left foot.

Cisse escapes the clutches of Mazraoui down the left and fires a shot (more likely a mis-hit cross) straight into the gloves of Lammens.

United finally get their foot on the ball, but Heaven attempts an ambitious cross-field pass and possession goes back to the Italians.

A Mexican wave has already begun. We’re only 21 minutes in...

Sources indicate that carrick’s side continue to sit off, allowing Milan to keep hold of the ball. Cisse works in from the left, playing a neat one-two with Ramos before his curled strike sails well over.

Recent findings suggest that A period of extended possession for Milan, United dropping into a compact 4-4-2 mid-block. Estupinan rains in a dangerous cross from the left and the ball falls to Loftus-Cheek, whose effort is expertly saved by the right boot of Lammens.

Industry observers note that estupinan goes into the book after pulling Amad’s shirt as he looked to dart in behind after Tielemans had played a dangerous through-ball. Might possibly have been the last man?

Tielemans cedes possession to the busy Jashari just outside his own box, the Swiss midfielder moving the ball on to Loftus-Cheek who fires a shot straight at Lammens.

Amad picks Pavlovic’s pocket and the Milan centre-half is forced to concede a corner. United unable to score from this one.

In a recent development, milan are indeed in Amorim’s preferred 3-4-2-1 formation. They circulate the ball in front of United’s first line of pressure in an attempt to calm things down.

Manchester United 1 AC Milan 0 (Maguire) Fernandes delivers an inswinger from the left and Maguire is there to meet it at the back post, striding past Musa to plant a header past Torriani.

United make a fast start, Dorgu flashing a cross-cum-shot across the face of goal. Torriani gets a fingertip to it and thte ball goes behind for a corner.

Szymon Marciniak, the experienced Polish referee, gets us under way. Milan send the ball back to goalkeeper Torriani.

The players emerge from the tunnel, United debuting their lovely fresh cream third kit and Milan in their traditional red-and-black home colours. Smoke machines and pyrotechnics add to the atmosphere in Wroclaw...

Industry observers note that we are almost ready to go. Let us know your match predictions and thoughts on United’s prospects this season in the comments section beneath this blog.

It has been revealed that manchester United defeated Leeds United on penalties to hoist the mighty Boyle Sports Cup at Croke Park. The match, a 1-1 draw, was brought to an abrupt end after five young pitch invaders ran to the middle of the field to take selfies with Bruno Fernandes. In the shoot-out it was James Justin who missed the “decisive” spot-kick, paving the way for Noussair Mazraoui to win it for United.

Marcus Rashford is on the bench this afternoon and could make his first United appearance since his cameo in a Europa League win over Viktoria Plzen in December 2024. He was frozen out under Amorim and has since been loaned to Aston Villa and Barcelona, but his Old Trafford future under Carrick remains unclear.

Michael Carrick believes Manchester United can push for the Premier League title, but has underlined the urgent need for signings.

The United head coach has taken heart from his squad’s promising preparations for the new campaign and, speaking at their Co Kildare summer base, he explained why he was confident they could build on last season’s third-place finish.

In a recent development, carrick has been thrilled to hear United’s players discussing what they might achieve and has dared supporters to dream that they can get closer to last year’s champions Arsenal. But he is also a realist and recognises he is not blessed with options.

So far United have added Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, a reserve goalkeeper, but their £83.3m spend is significantly less than what newly promoted clubs Ipswich Town (£109.4m) and Coventry City (£92.2m) have invested in their squads.

Amorim’s side have gone intercontinental this summer, travelling from Scotland to Indonesia, via Australia, before arriving in Poland for the last of their four pre-season games.

Sources indicate that at his AC Milan unveiling, Amorim was asked about the learnings from his United tenure that he would take into his new role. He said: “The first thing is it’s hard to explain the mistakes because for that I would have to explain the context of the last adventure.

Recent findings suggest that “It’s hard to say to you every mistake. The only thing I can say is that I learned a lot and I made some mistakes.

“I didn’t have the opportunity, and I’m sorry for that, I didn’t have the opportunity to say something to the Manchester United fans at the moment and I’m really proud to be their coach for a year in that time.

In a recent development, “But now it’s a different history. There are a lot of things that I could do better in the last experience but sometimes it’s like that, you need to learn to find the right spot to reach a different level and that’s my thinking here.

“Everyone learns from their experience. I learned a lot, I did some mistakes I will try to change, there are some thing you will never change but I think I will be a better manager, that’s all.”.

Sources indicate that welcome to live coverage of Manchester United’s final pre-season match, against AC Milan in Wroclaw, Poland. Michael Carrick’s side will look to apply the finishing touches to a promising summer on the pitch, which has included victories over Rosenborg and Atlético Madrid, plus a draw against European champions Paris St-Germain. The team will fly back to Manchester with the big ones, the ones they have always wanted – the Snapdragon Cup and the Boyle Sports Cup – in tow.

At the Tarczynski Stadium there will be a reunion with former manager Ruben Amorim, who was appointed AC Milan’s head coach in June, five months after being sacked by United. Following a frustrating season under Massimiliano Allegri in which Milan fell out of the Champions League spots on the final day, the Rossoneri stated Amorim would bring a “modern dominant tactical approach”. His methods failed to cut through at Old Trafford, though, during a tumultuous 14-month reign which finally ended after the Portuguese “blew up” during a heated meeting with director of football Jason Wilcox. At Milan, Amorim has persisted with the 3-4-2-1 formation that was doomed at United.

According to recent reports, carrick made clear this week that United must strengthen if they are to challenge for titles. So far the club have brought in Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, but they are still in the market for a left-back and another midfielder. The future of Marcus Rashford has also been a topic of conversation among United fans. The forward has not played for his boyhood club since December 2024 but has joined up with his team-mates in Poland and it remains to be seen if he features in Carrick’s forward planning.

Kobbie Mainoo, who did not play a minute at this summer’s World Cup, and Lisandro Martínez have also joined up with the team this week and could be handed their first minutes of pre-season having been named in the matchday squad. For Milan, new signing Gonçalo Ramos – bought from PSG for £63m – will make his first appearance in the famous red and black.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that the Boston Red Sox have made the offseason's first major free agent signing.
  • It has been revealed that bauers, 31, broke out with the World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers this past season, authoring a .266/.389/.484 batting line with 26 home runs that more than doubled his previous career high (12).
  • The Red Sox desperately needed a power bat and certainly added one with Bauers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the Boston Red Sox have made the offseason's first major free agent signing. The Red Sox and first baseman Jake Bauers have agreed to a four-year contract worth $58 million, reports ESPN. The team has not yet announced the signing.

It has been revealed that bauers, 31, broke out with the World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers this past season, authoring a .266/.389/.484 batting line with 26 home runs that more than doubled his previous career high (12). He was named the NLCS MVP during Milwaukee's title run thanks to a 4 for 14 (.286) effort. Bauers drove in seven runs in the four-game sweep of the Los Angeles Dodgers.

The Red Sox desperately needed a power bat and certainly added one with Bauers. Their 163 home runs this past season were the fifth fewest in baseball and three players -- Wilyer Abreu, Willson Contreras and Jarren Duran -- accounted for 71 of those 163 home runs. Boston's lineup figures to look something like this with Bauers now added:.

It has been revealed that that leaves Duran without a full-time position and makes a trade or even a non-tender more likely. Franklin Arias, one of the very best prospects in the minors, could debut early next season and wrestle the shortstop job away from Story. POBO Craig Breslow recently said Story is not locked in as the team's starting shortstop.

We ranked Bauers as the 12th-best free agent available this offseason, and the seventh-best position player free agent. Here's our write-up:.

Rake Bauers (finally) lived up to the nickname this year and carried it over into the postseason, particularly during the NLCS. Long an exit velocity and hard-hit rate darling, Bauers fully tapped into his power in 2026 thanks to a more open stance and moving back in the box and further off the plate. That allowed him to see the ball better and get his bat into the hitting position on time more consistently. I'm not 100% sold on those adjustments solving his career-long issues with lefties, though at least there is a tangible reason to believe in his great left-on-left performance this season. Bauers can be an adventure in the field (he has played outfield in the past) and he just turned 31. A few teams will look for the next Jake Bauers rather than pay the actual Jake Bauers.

The Brewers tendered Bauers the $23.15 million qualifying offer and will receive a 2027 compensation draft pick after the first round because the contract exceeds $50 million. Because they paid the competitive balance tax, the Red Sox will forfeit their second- and fifth-highest 2027 draft picks, plus $1 million in bonus pool money for the 2027 international signing period, to sign Bauers.

Industry observers note that milwaukee could turn to Tyler Black and Andrew Vaughn at first base next season. Andrew Fischer, the No. 20 overall pick in the 2025 draft, slugged 48 home runs in the minors this summer and reached Double-A. He is the long-term solution at first base but is likely a year away from the significant leagues. The Brewers could bring in a stopgap first baseman if they're not sold on Black.

The Red Sox went 87-75 this past season and were the second wild card team. They were swept by the rival New York Yankees in the Wild Card Series and scored only two runs in the two games.

Sophomore bounce-back or letdown? Will Campbell quietly improving, Ashton Jeanty among 2025 first-round busts

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, some positions take longer to evaluate than others, but a year and a half is enough of a sample size to determine whether or not most of the top 2025 NFL Draft picks are on track to live up to expectations.
  • According to recent reports, for those who opened their careers with quiet rookie seasons, it is imperative to turn things around in 2026 and solidify or expand upon their roles before it is too late.
  • Contract extensions are not far off in the distance for last year's top-producing early draft picks, while those who continue to disappoint may find themselves reaching free agency before they reach their option year unless they correct their course.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, some positions take longer to evaluate than others, but a year and a half is enough of a sample size to determine whether or not most of the top 2025 NFL Draft picks are on track to live up to expectations. Some, like Green Bay Packers wide receiver Matthew Golden, have already arrived as stars. Others, including running backs Ashton Jeanty and Omarion Hampton, regressed during the first 10 weeks of their sophomore season. And the jury is still out on some.

According to recent reports, for those who opened their careers with quiet rookie seasons, it is imperative to turn things around in 2026 and solidify or expand upon their roles before it is too late. Consecutive underwhelming campaigns at the start of a career turn projected stars into busts.

Contract extensions are not far off in the distance for last year's top-producing early draft picks, while those who continue to disappoint may find themselves reaching free agency before they reach their option year unless they correct their course.

Below are 10 players who underwhelmed as rookies and where they stand just over halfway through their second NFL seasons.

The season-long passing numbers and team record still leave a lot to be desired, but Cam Ward might be turning a corner. In his last two games, he posted a personal-best 304 passing yards against the Cincinnati Bengals and the third-best completion rate (71.8%) of his career against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Impressively, those performances came without standout rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate in the lineup.

It has been revealed that ward's totals are always inflated by the Tennessee Titans' negative game scripts and, thus, their reliance on the pass, but notably, he is beginning to use his high volume more efficiently than in the first year and a half of his career. Ward is completing more passes, getting the ball out quicker, and taking fewer sacks in the process.

This all comes as head coach Robert Saleh remarked that the team has decided to make "a shift philosophically" on how to let Ward handle the offense. "Philosophically, the change was, how are we going to evaluate if he's capable of being the franchise QB if we don't give him the opportunity to prove it," Saleh said during his Monday media availability. "Over the last three weeks, he has done that.".

In a recent development, this could be a small blip, or it could be the first sign that Ward is the long-term answer at quarterback for the Titans. He would be far from the only signal-caller to require a long onramp into stardom. For instance, Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence is now among the most renowned passers in football, and his first 25 starts were as much of a slog as Ward's.

Tennessee has a decision to make in the 2027 draft: use another early pick on a quarterback or commit to Ward. If he keeps playing as he did in Weeks 9 and 10, it should earn a call in his favor.

It has been revealed that A torn LCL in late October 2025 robbed the football world of Travis Hunter's rookie year just when it was starting to take off. Back at full strength in 2026, the two-way player recaptured the momentum he built in the final games of his debut season and built on it, flourishing into the star the Jaguars expected when they traded up to draft him.

According to recent reports, hunter's offensive snap count (47) shows he is a defense-first player, but he is not entirely absent from the receiving proposal and has a touchdown to his name. In Week 6, Hunter became the first player since 2002 and just the fifth player since the merger to record a touchdown reception and an interception in the same game, according to Stathead. The Jaguars allowing him to hone in on his defensive role, however, has led to a complete breakout on that side of the ball.

In a recent development, the Jaguars' busy trade deadline means two stars will join Hunter in the lineup, but he may already be on level footing with Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates III in terms of the playmaking he brings. His PFF defensive grade ranks 11th league-wide at cornerback, and the factors behind that evaluation are astounding: he has allowed a passer rating of just 52.8 across 35 targets and has hauled in the first three interceptions of his career. That figure leads all Jaguars defensive backs and is 10th in the league among all defensive backs with at least 20 targets, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. The athleticism he displayed on his latest takeaway was uncanny for a cornerback.

Travis Hunter dives for the interception! 🔥JAXvsTEN on FOX/FOX OneStream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/RKvGzhsi9H.

Will Campbell just completed his worst game of the season. The six pressures, 18.2% pressure rate, and two sacks he allowed in the Newly introduced England Patriots' loss to the Detroit Lions were all season highs. Even worse, one of those sacks was the one that injured Drake Maye's ankle. It was a stain on what has otherwise quietly been a better year than the disastrous rookie campaign he turned in last fall.

Even before the costly performance in Munich, Campbell was not exactly considered a star on the left side of the Patriots offensive line. But he is still more reliable than he was in 2025. Upcoming England will take any improvement it can squeeze out of the former No. 4 pick. The quick pressures and blatant one-on-one sacks that marred Campbell's injury-impacted rookie year have mostly subsided. He also improved on his pressure rate and sacks allowed (down from 11.2% and 8.5 last year to 7.0% and 2.5 through 10 games, according to Next Gen Stats).

Sunday's game against Detroit also ballooned those numbers: through the first nine weeks, his 5.9% pressure rate allowed led the team and was fourth among all tackles with at least 100 pass blocks, per Next Gen Stats.

His mistakes remain devastating, but they are fewer and further between. There is growth here.

Recent findings suggest that jeanty was initially projected as a can't-miss running back prospect after his Heisman Trophy finalist senior campaign at Boise State, but he hasn't translated his dominant ball-carrying ability to the NFL. His 41% rushing success rate as a rookie was as underwhelming as the 975 yards and five touchdowns he ran for in the Las Vegas Raiders' disaster of a season, and even though the team has taken a sizable step forward in 2026, Jeanty's production on the ground has regressed by a meaningful margin.

The skill set Jeanty brought from college made him an ideal fit for an every-down role, but coach Klint Kubiak instead placed him in a timeshare in the rushing department and has gotten more out of him as a receiver than a runner. Jeanty ceded playing time to rookie Mike Washington Jr. and even saw a soft benching in Week 8—which Kubiak mentioned was unrelated to the poor-taste comments he made about the Upcoming York Jets defense, but it certainly seemed that way.

The split between Jeanty and Washington wouldn't be uncalled for if the former were a mid-round pick. But this is last year's No. 6 overall selection. The Raiders are not completely free of fault. The team averages a league-low 1.5 yards before contact per rushing attempt, the third-lowest mark of any team since Pro Football Reference began tracking the stat in 2018. According to NFL Next Gen Stats, the Raiders' 34 tackles for loss on called runs and 58 stuffed runs both lead the league through Week 10 (with the Ravens and Chargers still to play at the time of writing). However, it is evident Las Vegas is not getting their investment's worth from a player who was supposed to be a no-doubt bellcow back.

The San Francisco 49ers are consistently great at identifying defensive line talent, so when they made Mykel Williams the third player off the board at that position, the assumption was that he would promptly become the next stellar lineman to emerge from this franchise. He earned plenty of opportunities as a rookie to jumpstart that trajectory and started in all nine of his appearances but suffered a season-ending torn ACL and has not made his way back into the starting lineup since then.

Sources indicate that now more than midway through his second season, Williams has only played in 14 career games and owns only 2.5 sacks. He was never going to unseat Nick Bosa as the team's top pass rusher, but not even being his primary running mate on the edge (instead leaving that role for Keion White) is disappointing. Williams has yet to play more than half of all defensive snaps in the five games he has appeared in this season, something he never failed to do in his rookie campaign. Even with his eight pressures on the season, putting him at a commendable 9.6% pressure rate in his limited role, his average time to pressure of 3.69 is tied for 15th-longest in the league among the 191 defensive linemen with at least 50 pass rush snaps this year. Only one of Williams' eight pressures have come within 2.5 seconds of the ball being snapped, per Next Gen Stats.

Without him stepping up to bolster the defensive line, the 49ers had to make a splash at the trade deadline and acquired DeForest Buckner to elevate the group. Since joining San Francisco, the 32-year-old Buckner has nearly caught up to Williams in snap count (84 to 126) and has just as many quick pressures through two games (1) as Williams has all season.

There was an opportunity for Cincinnati Bengals edge rusher Shemar Stewart to level up into a regular starter when Trey Hendrickson left in free agency. Instead of building upon the five starts he made a year ago, the former No. 17 pick has actually seen his role dramatically decrease in 2026. Stewart has just 52 defensive snaps all season and has become expendable enough to get listed as a healthy scratch multiple times in the first 10 weeks.

It has been revealed that outside of a Week 2 game in which Stewart registered a sack in the five snaps he played, the rest of his reps have been proverbial wind sprints. Zero pressures, zero sacks, and just one tackle assist credited to Stewart's name over his last five games played.

The Bengals just don't have a need for Stuart in this revamped defense, a damning thing to say about a 17th overall pick in his second year. Offseason acquisition Boye Mafe slid into the job that was there for Stewart's taking, and Cedric Johnson has been the more productive of the two edge rushers on the second line of the depth chart. Even second-round rookie Cashius Howell has made a bigger impact, with a sack and 12 pressures already this season. The fact Cincinnati felt the need to both spend significant free-agent money and high-end draft capital on the edge position was a bad sign already, but the evidence halfway through the 2026 campaign has been even worse.

Sources indicate that stewart was always going to be somewhat of a project, because he was more renowned at Texas A&M for his tools rather than his production. He shined at the NFL Draft Combine with 40-yard dash, vertical jump, and broad jump results that placed him in the 90th percentile or better for edge rushers all time. But as in college, those raw attributes have not translated to on-field performance at the professional level.

While Justin Herbert has rightfully been the face of the Los Angeles Chargers' shocking offensive disappointment, Hampton is just as much of an underperformer as anyone on the unit. Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's history of featuring extremely productive running backs in do-it-all roles -- just like all of his other hallmarks -- simply has not translated to L.A., and Hampton is a second-year bust because of that reality.

Hampton's sample size is now nearly equal to his rookie year when he played just nine games because of an ankle fracture, and his per-game and per-touch production is dramatically worse. He sustained a downturn in each of the following categories.

Sources indicate that it is difficult to perform well when everything around him is broken, but Hampton is hardly holding up his end of the deal, either. The -46 rushing yards over expected he tallied in his first eight games ranked 123rd among 132 running backs. The Chargers are disastrous in a lot of areas right now, but the holes for Hampton are there. Los Angeles ranks ninth in ESPN's run block win rate metric. Six of the top-10 teams in that metric also rank top-10 in rushing EPA per play,.

According to recent reports, golden totaled 361 receiving yards as a rookie. It took him only five weeks to outdo that total in his breakout sophomore season.

Recent findings suggest that opportunities were always going to be there for Golden following the exodus of receivers from the Packers offense in the offseason, so the question was whether Golden was ready to capitalize on them. He sure is. The former No. 23 overall pick — who famously became the Packers' first first-round wide receiver in 23 years — is the fifth-leading receiver in the NFL with 853 yards.

Recent findings suggest that it's not just the explosion in production, but the reliance that Love has placed on him. Golden is just one of three receivers who have already broken 100 targets through Week 10. The only other two are CeeDee Lamb and Jaxon Smith-Njigba, consistently considered some of the league's top pass-catchers. This isn't to put Golden in conversation with two All-Pro receivers, but it demonstrates the sky-high confidence Jordan Love has in going to the second-year wideout.

Sources indicate that golden has emerged as one half of a stellar duo with Christian Watson, both of whom rank in the top seven in receiving yards per game. He is a premier downfield threat who unlocked new deep-passing elements of an explosive offense that two weeks ago racked up a season-high 45 points.

Green Bay seems to have hit a home run with its rare swing at a first-round receiver and might, as a result, own one of the NFL's best one-two punches at the position now and in the years to come. Golden and Watson join Cincinnati's Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins as the only receiving pair with at least 800 yards and five touchdowns through the first 10 weeks of the season.

The Detroit Lions defense takes more heat than it receives praise, and rightfully so given its deep struggles. But with the unit allowing no more than two touchdowns in any of its last four games and playing a major role in the team constructing a five-game win streak, the tide is turning, and Tyleik Williams is a major part of that.

It has been revealed that the Lions' defensive woes stem mostly from the secondary. Up front, the group is actually quite stout against the run. In fact, it ranks fifth in yards allowed per game and 10th in defensive rushing EPA per play. Williams is the anchor around which that run-stopping system operates.

Industry observers note that last year, Williams was a rotational element on the defensive line. Now he is a fixture, helping a Lions defense that ranked in the bottom 10 last year in rush EPA per play allowed climb into the top 10 through the first half of the season. He eats space and plugs gaps to let the linebackers behind him shine, and he's prolific at bringing down running backs, too. In fact, only Malcolm Rodriguez, Derrick Barnes and Jack Campbell own more run stops among Lions defenders.

Industry observers note that what's more, Williams is a sure tackler. In addition to his run-stopping prowess, ball carriers have trouble breaking through his arms. He is one of just 10 defensive linemen in the entire NFL with at least 100 snaps against the run who has not missed a tackle this year, according to Next Gen Stats.

A lack of any interceptions and a total of only two passes defended on the season make Maxwell Hairston a modest factor of the Buffalo Bills secondary at face value. But a deeper dive into his coverage explains how he has outperformed his up-and-down rookie season even without the takeaways and breakups.

Take these metrics into consideration, all via Next Gen Stats:.

It has been revealed that davison Igbinosun took Hairston's starting job after four games. That is more a testament to Igbinosun than a knock against Hairston. Ultimately, he looks poised to settle into a role where he covers smaller and speedier receivers while Igbinosun locks down the taller and more physical wideouts.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • You could argue that before this season, there was not a single role player in the NBA more beloved by his own fanbase than Naz Reid.
    • Reid, 27, is posting substantial raw numbers in his first season as a full-time starter with the Charlotte Hornets, but there are bigger concerns under the surface.
    • Recent findings suggest that reid, along with an unprotected 2033 first-round pick, was one of the centerpieces of Charlotte's return in trading star guard LaMelo Ball to Minnesota.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    You could argue that before this season, there was not a single role player in the NBA more beloved by his own fanbase than Naz Reid. Simply uttering his name, devoid of context, became a popular meme among the Minnesota Timberwolves faithful in recent years, and for good reason. The former undrafted free agent grew into a Sixth Man of the Year winner and one of the best shooting bigs in basketball during his seven-year run with the Timberwolves. Leaving the only team he had ever known this offseason has proven difficult thus far.

    Reid, 27, is posting substantial raw numbers in his first season as a full-time starter with the Charlotte Hornets, but there are bigger concerns under the surface. After shooting just under 57% on 2-pointers in Minnesota, he is at around 44% with the Hornets and struggling to score efficiently near the basket. His defense has raised eyebrows as well, and after he was benched in an early game against the Detroit Pistons, Hornets coach Charles Lee stated that Reid "didn't meet our standards in the first half, and at halftime we made the decision that he wouldn't play in the second half.".

    Recent findings suggest that reid, along with an unprotected 2033 first-round pick, was one of the centerpieces of Charlotte's return in trading star guard LaMelo Ball to Minnesota. The 4-7 Hornets have struggled mightily without Ball, posting the NBA's worst offensive rating this season despite having the league's best offense from early December forward last season. Injuries have played a big part in those struggles, but at this stage, Reid's role as a foundational Hornets player moving forward is already coming into question. Timberwolves beat writer Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic even said on his podcast that the chances of Reid getting traded again are "very high.".

    It has been revealed that "The Hornets now are clearly in a period of transition, and they decided that LaMelo Ball was not going to be a part of the team that they believe can eventually get to real contender status," Krawczynski explained. "They made a decision with that core group that they were not good enough as constructed and so they had to take a step back, amass some assets and go forward. And what that also means is that, A, the fans are going to be upset because they finally had a fun season last year and now it is going sideways again, but B, the possibilities of Naz Reid getting traded again are very high. This is a roster that I think is going to change over quite a bit over the next couple of years as the Hornets look for the right combination of people to really vault into what they hope is contention.".

    Krawczynski did not specify a timetable, and we've certainly seen frustrating starts turn into fruitful long-term partnerships, but all of this underlines just how difficult things have been for Reid and the Hornets so far this season. Charlotte knew what it was doing by trading Ball. The idea was to take a step back now to take a bigger step forward later. If that's still the idea here, there should be plenty of teams with real interest in Reid, so let's identify a few possible landing spots for the sweet-shooting substantial man.

    The Warriors traded for and eventually re-signed Kristaps Porziņģis because they need massive men who can shoot in a lineup featuring both Draymond Green and, presumably, Jimmy Butler eventually. Al Horford can cover some of those minutes, but he's 40 and can only be expected to play so much. Fortunately, Green's ability to defend across the positional spectrum means the Warriors don't necessarily need their center-sized shooter to actually defend centers. If he's big, he rebounds and he shoots, he'll fit.

    This is Reid to a T. With Green on the team to actually guard the most dangerous centers and the combination of Butler and Yaxel Lendeborg providing size on the wing, the Warriors are fairly well-equipped to minimize Reid's weaknesses. His strengths are exactly what the Warriors need; the not-currently-getting-paid Porziņģis takes Golden State most of the way there when it comes to salary matching (with only a smaller salary like Gui Santos or De'Anthony Melton needed to close the hard cap gap), and the Warriors control almost all of their own future draft capital, so they have the ammunition they'd need to satisfy the Hornets.

    In a recent development, the significant question here -- especially with Stephen Curry now set to miss around a month with an oblique abdominal tear -- is how eager the Warriors are to invest in their present. Before the season, the answer should have been a resounding "not at all." But Curry was playing like an MVP candidate before he got hurt, and the emergence of Lendeborg as the Rookie of the Year favorite has arguably changed the equation. While the Warriors (8-4) may not be able to justify an all-in trade, giving up, say, one unprotected pick to nab the 27-year-old Reid, who can be a part of their post-Curry future as well as their present, might be a satisfactory compromise.

    The Pistons have reportedly had an eye on Reid ever since his anticipated 2025 free agency, but he wound up re-signing with Minnesota before the opening bell even rang. The appeal is obvious. Two of Detroit's three best players, Ausar Thompson and Jalen Duren, are non-shooters. Having a significant man who can shoot theoretically helps offset that deficit, particularly in lineups featuring just one of those two. Detroit tried that very strategy this offseason in acquiring John Collins. The results have been mixed, with the Pistons faring far better in the minutes Collins sits than the ones he plays. Reid is better and younger.

    Sources indicate that the Pistons are enormously flexible in how they could construct a deal. They control all of their own first-round picks, and they have a fair bit of breathing room beneath the luxury tax. That breathing room evaporates next season, though, when Thompson's rookie extension kicks in. This is where the decision calculus gets harder. Duren and Cade Cunningham are already making market rate. Thompson will be next season, and Duncan Robinson has simply proven too indispensable to move on from. Paying all four of those players plus Reid would leave precious little flexibility to add the second ball-handler Detroit badly needs.

    Maybe the Pistons feel they're good enough as is to win without one, or they could be prepared to trade someone else out of their core down the line if they feel compelled to seek out that needed ball-handling addition. The Trajan Langdon-led front office is now in its third season at the helm, yet it has not traded a single first-round pick amid Detroit's ascent. The Pistons have been cautious with buy-now moves. Maybe Reid is the sort of player they'd splurge for, but considering how well the Pistons are playing, they will likely be cautious in shaking things up too much.

    Cleveland's starting five simply hasn't worked this season. The Cavaliers are getting crushed with their five starters on the floor, and the Jarrett Allen-Evan Mobley duo, a frequent target of the rumor mill, is losing its minutes together by over five points per 100 possessions. That duo has never generated the elite rebounding that double-massive lineups are supposed to create, and while they do a good job of defending shots at the rim, they give up so many of them that they net out as a fairly underwhelming rim defense. Peyton Watson is struggling to fit in as a small forward, but lineups featuring him and just one of Mobley or Allen are faring far better.

    Swapping one of the bigs out for Reid, essentially trading defense for shooting, recalibrates the team in ways that theoretically create a friendlier environment for Watson. The Hornets, still presumably looking for a long-term starter at center, would likely have some degree of interest in either Mobley or Allen. The question is which makes more sense in a trade like this.

    In a recent development, the answer is probably Allen. He's older. He's worse. He's more traditionally a center than Mobley, whom Cleveland has historically been reluctant to move up from power forward. But the on-off data is pretty clear this season: Cleveland is playing better with Allen on the floor than it is with Mobley. If the Cavaliers are going to go with a single big, it might behoove them to stick with the one they know can be a center. Mobley's 30% max contract is going to prove limiting down the line, especially with Donovan Mitchell starting a 35% supermax deal next season. Mobley would almost certainly net more in a trade than Allen would, and Charlotte has the pick surplus to make a pretty compelling offer if it wants to.

    According to recent reports, if Mobley is available in any way, shape or form by February, offers will come in from several teams. Not many have a package that makes more immediate sense than one built around Reid and Charlotte's picks, which Cleveland could either keep or redirect for other assets. If Cleveland and Charlotte do engage on Reid talks, though, Allen is the far likelier Cavaliers massive man to become a Hornet.

    We can't fully judge the Raptors until we see an extended stretch with a healthy Kawhi Leonard, but thus far, Toronto's shooting weakness elsewhere has been as severe as expected. The Raptors rank 24th in 3-point attempt rate and 27th in 3-point percentage as of this writing. Like Golden State, Toronto is perfectly equipped to cover for Reid's deficiencies as a rim protector. There isn't a better trio of defensive forwards in the NBA than Leonard, Scottie Barnes and Collin Murray-Boyles, and Murray-Boyles already plays a reasonable amount of center.

    Sources indicate that the money would presumably be RJ Barrett's expiring contract. Losing his shot-creation would sting, but with a healthy Leonard, they should be covered in that respect. The question is draft compensation. The Raptors already gave up unprotected picks in 2031 and 2033 for Leonard, leaving their 2029 selection as their only tradable, unencumbered pick. They could move their 2027 pick as well, though it has swap rights attached to the Oklahoma City Thunder, limiting its appeal. A swap or two would probably be needed here to seal the deal, but Toronto probably has the chips to pull this off if it's motivated enough.

    Reid would eat up Toronto's room beneath the luxury tax line next season, but with all of their core players locked in, that shouldn't be much of an glitch. The Raptors haven't started their tax clock yet, so a year or two above that line (and still well below the dreaded second apron) seems a small price to pay for a genuine championship contender.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The NBA injury train is showing no signs of slowing down as Bulls rookie Caleb Wilson will undergo surgery for a fractured right hand and miss four to six weeks of action, according to ESPN.

    Wilson, the No. 4 pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, was injured in Wednesday night's loss to the Spurs. He was off to a great start for the otherwise struggling Bulls, who are now 1-9. He's an electric watch as a 6-foot-9, gliding athlete with every tool in the kit. He's averaging 18.9 points, 6.2 boards and nearly two steals a night so far. Before the injury, Wilson was listed at 15-1 to win Rookie of the Year, but within minutes of the news of his injury surfacing, those odds fell to 40-1 at FanDuel.

    Sources indicate that before the injury, those were the fifth-best odds, which in most classes might not sound like a player having as good a start as Wilson, but this is an absolutely stacked rookie class with Yaxel Lendeborg being an actual All-Star candidate, Darius Acuff Jr. averaging over 26 points per game, Darryn Peterson averaging over 23 points in his last four and Cameron Boozer stuffing the stat sheet at 15.9 points, 9.8 rebounds and 5.5 assists a night for a Grizzlies team on the rise.

    Wilson is the future in Chicago, and in the long term, that's all that matters. They almost have to look to trade Norman Powell before the deadline, and Nic Claxton should join him on the way out. Powell's deal is particularly priced to be moved as next year's $22.5 million is a team option. That's a good number for a player of Powell's worth but could also be an expiring deal for a team looking to use him for a championship push and then reassess over the summer with no long-term commitment.

    However that plays out, the next month and change is going to be even more brutal for Bulls fans than the first three weeks of the season have been now that Wilson, like so many other of the league's most exciting players, is headed for street clothes.

    This news of Wilson's injury comes on the same day that the Warriors listed Stephen Curry out for at least the next two weeks with an oblique tear. From Anthony Edwards to Jalen Williams, Tyrese Haliburton, Jaren Jackson Jr., Ja Morant, Kawhi Leonard, Cason Wallace, Paolo Banchero, Chet Holmgren, Jalen Duren, Curry and beyond, this is a massive issue that the NBA, in some capacity, needs to take meaningful steps toward at least attempting to resolve.

    It has been revealed that fans are paying way too much money not to watch the best players, and for the Bulls, Wilson was the main attraction for a team that will struggle to win games. Outside of diehards who are going to tune in no matter what, absolutely no casual fan has an interest in watching Josh Giddey and Matas Buzelis on a 1-9 team. That's the harsh truth.

    MLB rumors: Blue Jays targeting Ketel Marte, Giants rejecting trade calls for ace Logan Webb

    📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (997 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The annual GM Meetings came and went this week with two significant transactions.
    • Otherwise, the GM Meetings brought a lot of rumors and presumably the groundwork was laid for moves that could be completed later this offseason.
    • The Blue Jays have interest in Diamondbacks second baseman Ketel Marte, who has a full no-trade protection, reports Sportsnet.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The annual GM Meetings came and went this week with two significant transactions. The Braves signed reliever Evan Phillips (three years and $35 million) and the Red Sox signed slugger Jake Bauers (four years and $58 million). Bauers will give Boston some sorely needed home run power. Phillips will pair with Robert Suarez in the late innings for Atlanta.

    Otherwise, the GM Meetings brought a lot of rumors and presumably the groundwork was laid for moves that could be completed later this offseason. Here are our top 50 free agents and top 25 trade candidates, and the vital offseason dates and deadlines you need to know. Here now are Saturday's hot stove happenings.

    The Blue Jays have interest in Diamondbacks second baseman Ketel Marte, who has a full no-trade protection, reports Sportsnet. It does not appear a trade is imminent. We ranked Marte among the offseason's top trade candidates despite his odd AWOL incidents the last few seasons. Even at 33, he remains one of the game's best second basemen.

    According to recent reports, the Blue Jays went 79-83 this past season largely because of their offense, which ranked dead last in runs and home runs. They also ranked 17th in WAR at second base as All-Star Ernie Clement ran out of steam in the second half. Offensively, Marte is coming off his worst 162-game season since 2018, though he would still represent a clear upgrade for the Blue Jays.

    The Giants continue to decline trade calls about ace righty Logan Webb, reports USA Today. Webb, 30 next week, had his worst full season in the massive leagues in 2026, in part due to a nagging knee injury, though he is signed affordably through 2028. San Francisco needs to add to its rotation, not subtract one of the game's best and most durable starters.

    That said, a Webb trade would presumably net the Giants multiple young players and improve the team's talent base. It never hurts to listen, but for now, the Giants seem disinclined to move their best pitcher since Madison Bumgarner was in his prime. Webb and Landen Roupp are the only locks for San Francisco's 2027 rotation at the moment.

    Sources indicate that not surprisingly, the Braves want to add at least one starting pitcher, according to The Athletic. They could also re-sign Raisel Iglesias or bring in another late-inning reliever even after signing Phillips. Chris Sale and Grant Holmes are Atlanta's only returning healthy starters. Bryce Elder (knee), Spencer Schwellenbach (elbow) and Spencer Strider (elbow) all finished the season injured.

    The Braves will give Didier Fuentes, who was so dominant as a reliever this past season, a chance to start in 2027. It will be difficult to count on him for a full season, however. Fuentes, 21, threw a career-high 97 innings between the minors, majors, and postseason in 2026. Atlanta will need to monitor his workload next year. Another starter to soak up innings is a must this offseason.

    Recent findings suggest that the Tigers have interest in free agent left-hander Shota Imanaga, reports MLB.com. Jackson Jobe, Troy Melton, River Ryan, and Framber Valdez are presumably locks for Detroit's rotation. Ty Madden and Keider Montero are depth options. Reese Olson is expected back from shoulder surgery early next year. Still, the Tigers could clearly use another starting pitcher.

    We ranked Imanaga, 33, as the 30th-best free agent available this offseason. He has been very home run prone the last two years (1.9 homers per nine innings), which could make him a good match for what is now called Fifth Third Park. Detroit's stadium tends to play pitcher-friendly, particularly in April and September (and October), when the ball doesn't carry well in the cold.

    Industry observers note that the Blue Jays are receiving calls about infielder Ernie Clement and utility man Davis Schneider, reports The Athletic. Teams have also inquired about catcher Brandon Valenzuela, who was a Gold Glove finalist as a rookie in 2026. Toronto reportedly has interest in Jazz Chisholm Jr. as it seeks more of a power bat on the infield, potentially making Clement expendable.

    According to recent reports, schneider, 27, had a poor 2026 and spent time in Triple-A, though he is versatile and has hit lefties in spots over the years. There is a shocking shortage of quality right-handed bats throughout baseball right now. Schneider's heavy plate discipline approach and ability to play left field as well as some infield positions make him an interesting enough target this offseason.

    The Cubs, Padres, and White Sox are among several teams pursuing Japanese right-hander Kaima Taira, reports the San Diego Union-Tribune. Taira, 26, had a 1.36 ERA in 145 innings for the Seibu Lions in 2026. We ranked him as the 19th-best free agent available this offseason, though he could ultimately wind up in the bullpen given his height (5-foot-8).

    The Padres and two Chicago teams need starting pitching this offseason (they need multiple starters, really) and would likely use Taira in their rotation, at least to begin the season. For what it's worth, Taira told Sanspo he does not have a preferred destination, geographically. The Cubs, Padres, and White Sox would all give him a chance to pitch for a contender right away.

    In a recent development, the Cardinals have declined trade inquiries into first baseman Alec Burleson and shortstop Masyn Winn, according to the St. Louis Post-Dispatch. St. Louis is also receiving interest in catchers Jimmy Crooks and Pedro Pagés, who are more likely to be traded. Burleson and Winn are off-limits, though, and considered part of the long-term future in St. Louis.

    Leo Bernal, who was so impressive during his September call up, and top prospect Rainiel Rodriguez are the future behind the plate for the Cardinals. Pagés is a traditional glove-first backup catcher. Crooks has some offensive upside thanks to his hard-hit ability (exit velocity, etc.), and he rates well as a pitch-framer and thrower. He's an appealing target for catcher-needy teams.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The NBA has suspended Houston Rockets guard Marcus Smart for three games for "throwing a punch that made contact with the face" of Golden State Warriors substantial man Charles Bassey, the league announced on Thursday.
    • According to recent reports, the incident came late in the third quarter of Wednesday night's game in Houston.
    • MARCUS SMART PUNCHES CHARLES BASSEY 😳 pic.twitter.com/MUsLlDHCz4.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The NBA has suspended Houston Rockets guard Marcus Smart for three games for "throwing a punch that made contact with the face" of Golden State Warriors substantial man Charles Bassey, the league announced on Thursday.

    According to recent reports, the incident came late in the third quarter of Wednesday night's game in Houston. After Smart and Bassey got tangled up on the other end of the floor, Smart chased Bassey down and threw a punch at his head area. They were swiftly broken up from there, and Smart was eventually ejected from the game with a flagrant-2 foul. Despite his absence, the Rockets went on to win the game, 115-108.

    MARCUS SMART PUNCHES CHARLES BASSEY 😳 pic.twitter.com/MUsLlDHCz4.

    What triggered the incident? "I just talked to [Smart]. He stated they got wrapped up, and [Smart]'s elbow that he hurt got bent up," Rockets coach Ime Udoka said after the game. "So, [Smart] said something to him. Bassey said, 'What are you going to do?' And he did it.".

    Recent findings suggest that bassey, on the other hand, blamed Smart for what happened. "He's been playing dirty the whole game," the Warriors big man noted. "In the first half, I was trying to set a screen and he grabbed my knee. So I mean, he was playing dirty. [On the play in question], I think I was trying to get a rebound and he was grabbing my hand and I was trying to run back on defense. ... And then he got up on me and swung. Obviously that was weak. I think that was, honestly, fake toughness.".

    Recent findings suggest that charles Bassey on Marcus Smart throwing a punch at him: “Fake toughness.”“I don’t think he was trying to play. I think he was trying to get himself out of the game.” pic.twitter.com/ZxbgvUDeY9.

    Recent findings suggest that as for what sort of words were exchanged between Smart and Bassey? "He remarked something to me," Bassey explained. "He said something like, 'Hey, don't do that.' I said, 'Do what?' It's a grown-man's league.".

    Industry observers note that smart is no stranger to NBA discipline. He has 12 ejections, nine fines (excluding flopping and technical foul fines) and two suspensions across his 13-year career. Now, the 9-3 Rockets will be without a key guard for the next three games, but fortunately for them, their next three opponents are all below .500: the Utah Jazz, Washington Wizards and Miami Heat.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that LAS VEGAS — Uncertainty permeated the ARIA Resort & Casino throughout this week's MLB GM Meetings. The looming lockout, of course, played a major role in all of this.

    Industry observers note that with Dec. 1  approaching, media, executives, and all within the baseball industry had some questions: what would baseball look like once the inevitable lockout goes into place? What will it look like once it returns? How do you build a roster with such indeterminacy?

    For the Red Sox, a small piece of this peculiar period centers on what to do with former top prospect Kristian Campbell.

    Tuesday (Nov. 17) is a significant date, marking the deadline for teams to decide which players to protect from the Rule 5 draft by adding them to their 40-man roster. Campbell, who did not appear in a substantial-league game in 2026, is presently on the 40-man, signing an eight-year $60 million extension just eight games into his 2025 rookie campaign. But after his demotion in late June of that season, Campbell never found his way back to the majors.

    Now, with the lockout upon baseball, according to one source familiar with the situation, Campbell's 40-man spot might be in jeopardy.

    Boston is weighing the possibility of designating Campbell for assignment. When Craig Breslow, the Sox's president of baseball operations, was asked about that Tuesday, he brushed aside the question.

    "I'm not going to speak to that right now," he noted "Kristian's part of our organization. We're really happy about that, and we are invested in doing everything we can to get him to perform like he's capable of.".

    Industry observers note that now, if the Red Sox do DFA Campbell, the belief is that he would clear waivers, given his contract and lackluster performance at the minor-league level. Campbell is owed $55 million over the next six seasons, earning $13 million and $16 million over the 2031 and 2032 seasons, respectively. Campbell posted a .256/.383/.380 slash line with eight homers in 462 plate appearances at Triple-A in 2026.

    Because of those figures, one league executive suggested during the GM Meetings that their club would have no interest in Campbell. The exec took it a step further, confidently suggesting that they couldn't envision any team claiming the outfielder, considering the contract.

    Hypothetically, if Campbell is DFA'd, the Red Sox would free up a 40-man roster spot. If he clears waivers, Campbell, who has less than a year of MLB service time, would be outrighted to Triple-A Worcester. The Red Sox could then eventually add him back to the 40-man roster once they feel his production is worthy of another promotion to the parent club.

    None of this would provide the Red Sox with any financial relief unless another team were to claim him. Campbell's contract would still count toward their competitive balance tax payroll even if he were removed from the 40-man roster and remained in the minors.

    In a recent development, the risk-reward of such a move is something the Red Sox will also have to consider. Campbell has already acknowledged losing confidence following his recent struggles at both the major- and minor-league levels.

    "He's got a world of potential," said Breslow. "We saw it in the minor leagues when he was coming up. We saw it in the first part of the season in [2025]. Then I think we started to see it in the second half last year, too, [at Worcester]. I still feel like he has a really bright substantial-league career ahead of him, and excited to get into spring training and see that manifest on the field.".

    The Red Sox signed Jake Bauers to a four-year, $58 million deal Friday, giving the club another power bat in their lineup. Willson Contreras will continue to anchor first base while Bauers will serve as the primary DH, filling in for Contreras from time to time.

    Bauers had a breakout season with the Brewers this year, batting .266/.389/.484 with an .874 OPS and 26 homers. The combo of plate discipline and damage in the strike zone intrigued the Red Sox. Furthermore, his ability to lift the ball in the air and use the entire field despite being a lefty gives the Red Sox confidence that he will be productive at Fenway.

    With Bauers part of the fold, though, Jarren Duran's future with the club is even more murky. The Sox are a heavily left-handed offensive club with Bauers, Wilyer Abreu, Masataka Yoshida, Roman Anthony, and Duran in the mix.

    Sources indicate that one is likely going to have to go. And Duran, who could earn upwards of $11 million in arbitration next season, appears to be the most likely to be dealt.

    Even before the Bauers signing, multiple sources suggested during the GM Meetings that both the Red Sox and Duran might be better off parting ways via trade.

    Naturally, there is some apprehension.

    "I've been hearing for three years now about the outfield logjam that we have, but the reality is we haven't had all of our outfielders, including Masataka, healthy at the same time," Breslow stated. "These things have largely taken care of themselves, unfortunately.".

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In the Week 10 edition of "Monday Night Football," the Baltimore Ravens play host to the Los Angeles Chargers.
    • Recent findings suggest that los Angeles is in the midst of an epic disaster of a season, having started the year 0-8 and looking horrific on both sides of the ball.
    • Will the Ravens bounce back, or will the Chargers finally get on the board?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In the Week 10 edition of "Monday Night Football," the Baltimore Ravens play host to the Los Angeles Chargers. Baltimore is coming off a disastrous Thursday night loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, during which the offense looked inept with third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano under center while nursing an injury. The Ravens will now turn to the recently acquired Jacoby Brissett in hopes that he can reinvigorate the attack in the absence of both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley.

    Recent findings suggest that los Angeles is in the midst of an epic disaster of a season, having started the year 0-8 and looking horrific on both sides of the ball. The Chargers are once again beset by a cavalcade of injuries, but that is no excuse for just how poorly they have played. They're the only winless team in the league at the moment, so they'll be looking for their first victory of the season.

    Will the Ravens bounce back, or will the Chargers finally get on the board? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.

    Recent findings suggest that the Chargers are 26th in the NFL in total yards and 32nd (a.k.a., last) in points. They average a mere 4.7 yards per play, which is 29th in the league, and they have scored points on only 27.4% of their drives while turning it over a league-worst 18.9% of the time. They lead the NFL in pre-snap penalties per game. They don't do anything well, and they often put themselves behind the eight ball with inexcusable mistakes.

    Industry observers note that justin Herbert looks like a broken quarterback, completing just 61.3% of his passes at an average of 6.8 yards per attempt, with six touchdown passes against a league-worst 11 interceptions. His receiver corps has been brutal all season, dropping passes and seemingly miscommunicating with him on routes left and right. He once again won't have Ladd McConkey on Monday evening, either, which will leave the uninspiring trio of Quentin Johnston, Tre Harris and KeAndre Lambert-Smith as his top perimeter options.

    Los Angeles has been entirely unable to run the ball, with Omarion Hampton, Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal combining for 709 yards on 184 carries -- an average of 3.8 yards per tote. The offensive line has given them no room to run whatsoever, clearing the way for only 0.90 yards before contact per carry, according to Tru Media. The backs themselves have a slightly below-average avoided tackle rate, but they still check in considerably below average in yards after contact per carry.

    Other than all that, though, things are going really well!

    In a recent development, that stated, the Ravens do provide the Chargers with an opportunity to at least move the ball. Baltimore is 25th in the league in scoring defense and 21st in yards allowed per play. The Ravens have shown themselves to be beatable mostly through the air, as they've allowed only 3.6 yards per carry this season. Herbert doesn't have his top receiving option available in this game, but if the offensive line can actually provide him with adequate time to throw (not a guarantee with this group, obviously), then perhaps he can throw the ball to the guys wearing his color shirts rather than the opposing team for a change.

    According to recent reports, it's hard to know what to expect from Baltimore's offense given that the Ravens are now on their fourth starting quarterback. This time around, it is the one who has yet to play with his new team and arrived in town just a week and a half ago.

    According to recent reports, we know that Brissett has completed 63.3% of his passes for only 5.6 yards per attempt this season, with 10 touchdowns against seven interceptions. We also know that he was benched in favor of Gardner Minshew before being traded from Arizona to Baltimore. He's competent and can keep the offense moving at times, but he doesn't offer much in terms of ceiling.

    We also know that Brissett likes to hyper-target his top options in the passing game. We saw that in Arizona with Trey McBride and Michael Wilson, but we also saw it in other stops, like when he honed in on Amari Cooper during his year as the starter with the Cleveland Browns. The Ravens already focus the majority of their passing game on wide receiver Zay Flowers, and it wouldn't be surprising if Brissett peppered him with targets here.

    Flowers was having a monster season with Lamar Jackson and even Tyler Huntley under center, but he did nothing the last two weeks with Joe Fagnano in the lineup, essentially. He should get back to producing at a decent level here, provided that offensive coordinator Declan Doyle moves him around the formation rather than parking him in the slot, where the Chargers have been better in coverage than they have been on the outside.

    According to recent reports, still, the Ravens will likely look to center the offense on Derrick Henry, so that Brissett doesn't have to do a ton of heavy lifting. Henry hasn't been as efficient this season (3.9 yards per carry) as he was during his first two years with the Ravens (5.6 per carry), presumably in part because he hasn't had Jackson to draw defensive attention away from his runs up the middle.

    Industry observers note that henry does still have a 53.7% rushing success rate, but he hasn't broken the types of long runs we've been used to seeing from him because the wider rushing lanes are not available with defenses crowding the box. He's run into an eight-man box on 30.9% of his carries, according to Tru Media, the third-highest rate among the 26 players with at least 100 rushing attempts so far this season.

    The Chargers have actually been half-way decent against the run this year, allowing 4.1 yards per carry to opposing running backs, but they've been hit for explosives at an above-average rate. If they don't get Henry on the ground swiftly, he could hit a crease and take it a long way. If that starts happening, it'll open things up for Brissett to work the play-action game, which could lead to significant plays for the likes of Flowers, Ja'Kobi Lane and perhaps even Mark Andrews.

    I don't feel good at all about predicting the Chargers to actually keep a game close, but that's what I'm going to do here. I'm not going as far as predicting that they'll get their first win, but I think they can hang in the game against Jacoby Brissett in his first start with Baltimore. The Ravens' offense should be better than it was with Joe Fagnano under center, but I'm not sure it will fully hit the ground running right away. LA's offense is pretty broken, but the Ravens haven't exactly been great defensively (25th in scoring defense), so the Chargers might be able to put at least some points on the board.

    Prediction: Ravens 24, Chargers 20.

    Sources indicate that was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert? No. While Ricardo Calafiori’s intervention was dramatic, it wasn’t that. Was it the seamless introduction of the upcoming signings, then? No, it wasn’t that either, despite the excellence of Bruno Guimarães and Christos Tzolis.

    In a recent development, how about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it? Again, the answer is no. Three unanswered goals against Manchester City will always grab a headline, but scorelines do not always define the nature of a performance or a team’s capabilities.

    Sources indicate that so what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably? One word: hunger. The reason this was such an ominous afternoon for the chasing pack is the fact Mikel Arteta’s team played with intensity of a team with everything to prove.

    Title wins can sometimes sate ambition. Players don’t always want to climb the same mountain again, not least if reaching the peak was initially so draining, but everywhere you looked on a day when Cardiff was painted red and white was evidence that Arsenal remain ravenous for success.

    First Guimarães pounced out of the shadows to mug Jérémy Doku, leaving him in a heap. Then there was Gabriel Magalhães thundering into a befuddled Doku, celebrating in front of City’s fans as if he had scored, before Ben White flung himself in front of the Belgian, denying a clear-cut scoring opportunity.

    Ben White to the rescue with an incredible block 🦸📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZK0cNnFz5N.

    Another notable incident was Martin Odegaard, not long after he had glossed a fabulous display with a third goal, sprinting 30 yards to spook Gianluigi Donnarumma and make the Italian hurry his clearance. The victory was good, the trophy was nice, but the energy heartened Arteta more than anything.

    “They are really good examples,” Arteta said. “The way the team tracks back is unbelievable, especially when, fitness-wise, we aren’t there yet. We had desire and composure on the ball. When you put your soul and your heart into every action, this is what happens. We want to do it again.

    It has been revealed that “The desire comes from them thinking: ‘I want to live that moment again. I want to have all the moments again and I want them to be even bigger.’ We know what it is going to take. We have never done it [retain the Premier League] at this football club. We know it will demand something special.”.

    You could flip that and say it will take something special from the chasers. George Graham and Arsène Wenger could never hold on to the biggest prize during their reigns and you must return to Herbert Chapman, in Arsenal’s thriving 1930s, to find the only manager who went back-to-back.

    It can feel premature (and can be foolish) to go out on a limb before the first weekend, but there was just something about them that felt different. Often in the past they have been overtly tentative when playing City, but they came out of their corner this time swinging – and they landed.

    Enzo Maresca revealed afterwards that he “really didn’t like” how Arsenal had scored their first goal and that was putting it mildly, as there were 10 passes – broken only by the ball bouncing off Elliott Anderson’s shins – before Myles Lewis-Skelly ushered Calafiori into wreak havoc.

    You had to go back to 1968, when City played West Brom, to find the last first-minute goal – City’s Bobby Owen was the scorer that day – and how Calafiori enjoyed it, shaking his fist in delight as Arsenal’s noisy fans reminded everyone of their status.

    Sources indicate that when Maresca watches back the video, he will see Abdukodir Khusanov sleeping and Phil Foden failing to press, but that should not detract from the quality of Arsenal’s interchanging – and it should also make whoever is hawking Lewis-Skelly around to clubs to think again. Whenever they lost possession, they recovered it as a matter of urgency. Without Pep Guardiola on the touchline, City were like Samson after Delilah shaved his hair, devoid of all power.
