    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    So far, quarterback injuries and a revolving door of quarterbacks represent defining aspects of the 2026 NFL season. That number reached 50 quarterbacks in Week 10, which would be a staggering amount for an entire season.

    According to recent reports, so where do they all stack up? The rankings were broken down into 10 tiers, with three quarterbacks getting their own tier.

    According to recent reports, nobody wants to be here, but their performances have nonetheless left them in the basement. Of all the quarterbacks in this group, Herbert is the most notable given all the success he experienced during his first six seasons in Los Angeles.

    Herbert hasn't been good, but it's not all on him. His supporting cast hasn't carried its weight, and the Chargers' coaching staff (especially Jim Harbaugh and OC Mike McDaniel) aren't on the same page.

    Recent findings suggest that if there's a silver lining for Herbert, it's that Peyton Manning had a similar season at a similar point in his career. Manning bounced back all the way to the Hall of Fame. We'll see how Herbert responds to this adversity.

    Mendoza gets his own tier for two reasons: he's had just one start, and that start was a mixed bag. Overall, it was a promising debut for the No. 1 overall pick.

    Sources indicate that facing Seattle's "Dark Side" defense, Mendoza went 11 of 13 in the first half and scored the only touchdown before intermission on a 10-yard run. Mendoza was less effective in the second half as Seattle ratcheted up the pressure. He finished with 143 yards on 17 of 29 passing in a 21-13 loss.

    Each of these backups experienced various levels of success.

    McCarthy, traded from the Vikings to address New York's injury situation, is getting another chance (albeit temporary) to be an NFL starting quarterback. As was the case in Minnesota, McCarthy has shown signs of being a solid player in New York, but he still needs to work on his consistency, among other things.

    Take last week, for example. McCarthy threw for 293 yards and a touchdown and made some plays with his feet, but he also threw an ugly interception that sealed Upcoming York's loss to Washington.

    Recent findings suggest that daniels, the only rookie in this group, led the Buccaneers to their first win of the season, an upset in Dallas back in Week 5. A week later, he took Tampa Bay to overtime in an eventual loss to the Steelers.

    It has been revealed that mayfield was included here because his performance this season is most in line with this tier. He threw just 14 combined passes in his two wins as Tampa Bay's starting quarterback. He made odd history in Week 8 by becoming the first quarterback since 1974 to win a start without completing a single pass.

    These quarterbacks have had moments of success this season, but those moments have often been overshadowed by shortcomings.

    Hurts is dealing with something much bigger than football. He's been away from the team since blood clots were discovered following the Eagles' Week 5 loss to the Jaguars in London. The Eagles mentioned at the time that Hurts' prognosis is "very good" and that he is expected to make a full recovery.

    In a recent development, murray is listed as a starter here, but there's a very good chance that, barring injury, he has made his final start for the Vikings. Minnesota's production with him under center just wasn't up to snuff.

    It has been revealed that 22. Geno Smith, Jets     21. Drake Maye, Patriots.

    According to recent reports, 18. Aaron Rodgers, Steelers  17. Bryce Young, Panthers.

    Sources indicate that these guys aren't the first quarterbacks taken in fantasy football drafts, and for good reason: they don't consistently put up numbers. They are, however, above-average quarterbacks who once in a while show flashes of greatness, just not enough to be ranked higher.

    Recent findings suggest that rodgers' production isn't close to what it once was, but he has continued to play good football (especially for a 42-year-old) while helping the Steelers get off to a 6-3 start. A big reason Rodgers hasn't had more success is Pittsburgh's lack of receiving weapons, a need that wasn't addressed at the trade deadline.

    Nix had a slow start to the season, which was probably a byproduct of January's season-ending ankle injury. His play has improved in recent weeks, which is certainly good news for a Broncos team with Super Bowl aspirations.

    Watson has struggled with his consistency and production from a touchdown standpoint (he hasn't thrown a touchdown pass since Week 5), but he's been good enough to win six of his nine starts. Each of Cleveland's wins featured game-winning drives led by Watson.

    Maye's tumultuous season took a disastrous turn Sunday when he suffered a potentially season-ending ankle injury.

    Each backup quarterback that has started a game this season has had various levels of success. None has been better than Lock, who is 3-0 this year as Seattle's starting quarterback. Lock's stellar play (he has had seven touchdowns, no picks, and has completed 73.1% of his passes) has led to rumblings about whether or not he should be the starter in Seattle moving forward.

    It has been revealed that stroud has put up good numbers, and he is far from Houston's biggest problem. Houston had seven players miss Sunday's loss to Cleveland due to injury. Their running game has been largely non-existent, and the defense has underperformed all year.

    Prescott continues to be one of the league's most prolific passers, but most of his production has come against bad teams or when the Cowboys were trying to catch up, as was the case during Sunday's loss to the 49ers.

    In a recent development, cousins' performance in Sunday's win over the Packers was nothing short of amazing. Just days after being traded from Las Vegas, Cousins threw a pair of scores and completed 67.7% of his passes while leading Minnesota to a 30-10 win. If Cousins keeps this up, the Vikings could very well win the NFL's hardest division, if not the Super Bowl.

    Recent findings suggest that per usual, Daniels has been excellent this season when healthy. Dart was off to a strong start before an injury ended his sophomore season after just two weeks.

    Sources indicate that jackson was off to another strong start before a thumb injury derailed his season and the Ravens'. Williams missed three games earlier this season, and while his play has been mostly good, his production has been somewhat lacking (he has just three games with multiple touchdown passes this season). His four-pick performance in Chicago's Week 9 win over Tampa was a tough watch.

    Stafford, the league's reigning MVP, has displayed remarkable resilience this season amid the Rams' early losses and injuries to Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. He won't win a second MVP this season, but in some ways, Stafford's performance so far this season is just as impressive.

    In a recent development, stafford's predecessor in Los Angeles, Goff continues to play at a high level in Detroit. His success has led to continued success for the Lions, who are once again in the thick of the NFC North race.

    All five of these guys have an MVP case.

    Allen, the MVP front-runner for most of the season's first half, doesn't have as many touchdown passes (13) as his peers, but he does have a league-high 11 touchdown runs. He's also the catalyst for the Bills' 8-1 start.

    Purdy has been rock solid all year for the 8-1 49ers, but it's fair to wonder whether his strong supporting cast will negatively impact his MVP chances. Regardless, Purdy is playing the best ball of his career and is a big reason why the 49ers are the cream of the NFC crop.

    Sources indicate that love skyrocketed up the QB charts over the last six weeks prior to Sunday's setback to the visiting Vikings. Sunday's game exposed the Packers' beat-up offensive line and their lack of a running game without Josh Jacobs. Love is exceptional, but he can only do so much.

    Lawrence is a chameleon in that he can conform to whatever the Jaguars need him to be on a weekly basis in order to win. That's led to some gaudy games for Lawrence and other games where he has excelled in a supporting role. That has helped the Jaguars get to 7-2.

    In a recent development, mahomes earned a spot in this tier following his performances over the last three weeks. Outside of the No. 1 quarterback on our list, no quarterback has played better over that span than Mahomes. In the Chiefs' last three games, Mahomes has thrown 10 touchdowns, zero interceptions, completed 70% of his passes and averaged 304 passing yards per game. MVP-type stuff if you ask me.

    Already the MVP favorite entering Sunday night's game against the Steelers, Burrow is now the clear front-runner. Against a team that defeated the Bengals back in Week 3, Burrow threw for 409 yards and four touchdowns while completing nearly 80% of his passes.

    In a recent development, burrow's performance not only strengthened his MVP case but also put him on a historic trajectory with eight games to play in the 2026 regular season. He is one of only five quarterbacks in NFL history with over 30 total touchdowns through nine games, according to CBS Sports Research. The other four (Tom Brady in 2007, Rodgers in 2011, Peyton Manning in 2013 and Mahomes in 2018) won league MVP:.

    Industry observers note that burrow is on track to create his own category for quarterback excellence by becoming the first quarterback to throw for 5,000 yards and 50 touchdowns in a season while also completing 70% of his passes. If he does that, he will have a strong argument when it comes to having the greatest passing season in league history.

    Same old Spurs given reality check of epic proportions

    📅 22 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 25 min read (4996 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~25 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that the players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur.
    • Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.
    • But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that the players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur. The same Tottenham that finished each of the last two seasons in 17th. The same Tottenham that folded in adversity. The same Tottenham that opposition fans loved to laugh at.

    Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.

    But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.

    The Spurs supporters who have become sick of being made the butt of their rivals’ jokes had to listen to Brentford fans singing “Thomas Frank, he’s laughing at you” in reference to the Dane’s unhappy spell in north London.

    The impending arrival of Savinho will take Tottenham’s spending over £300m, but none of their big-money debutants at the Gtech Community Stadium hit the ground running.

    There was only one man who looked anything close to a £100m player and it was not Sandro Tonali.

    Tottenham’s first-ever £100m signing was completely upstaged by Brentford’s Mamadou Sangaré on his first competitive start for the club, as Spurs were run ragged.

    Sangaré might not have scored on his Brentford debut, but he had a major contribution in two of his side’s goals and bossed the middle of the park. He deservedly received a standing ovation when he was substituted with 15 minutes remaining.

    Recent findings suggest that “He is a top player, no doubt about it,” mentioned head coach Keith Andrews. “He is the one we were after in the window. The club deserve a lot of credit because a lot of clubs were looking at him.

    According to recent reports, “He deserves a lot of credit too, because he could have gone elsewhere for a few more bob. He recognised this would be a good place to come and he has settled quite nicely.”.

    A club-record £39m signing from French club Lens, Sangaré may prove to be a steal for Brentford. He ran the game for long periods and was responsible for Keane Lewis-Potter’s opening goal.

    Having played a lovely one-two with Dango Ouattara, Sangaré kept his cool to brilliantly pick out Lewis-Potter and give him the easy task of finding the back of the net.

    Keane Lewis-Potter scores Brentford's first goal of the fresh season!Brilliant play from record signing Mamadou Sangaré 👏 pic.twitter.com/Ua9HklQaWh.

    Later in the first half, Sangaré won a free-kick in his own half thanks to some quick feet and the action produced a big cheer from the home fans.

    Tonali was the subject of chants of “what a waste of money” from Brentford supporters. It was a volley that sailed high over the crossbar that prompted that particular song, but Tonali was not just off target with his shooting.

    It has been revealed that he lost possession on a couple of occasions at both ends of the pitch and allowed Brentford players to glide past him during the opening stages of the match. He struggled to get around the pitch and Tottenham generally lacked desire and fight – two things that clubs cannot buy.

    Recent findings suggest that richarlison, Lucas Bergvall and goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky can all be disappointed with Brentford’s second goal. Richarlison’s hold-up play was terrible, Bergvall produced a weak challenge that allowed Mathias Jensen to take the ball and shoot, and Kinsky parried the ball straight into the path of Vitaly Janelt, who scored.

    Kinsky has been trusted to take over from Guglielmo Vicario as Tottenham’s number one this season, but this was not a good start.

    Sources indicate that vitaly Janelt doubles Brentford's lead! 🐝 pic.twitter.com/AYh5BGhJBQ.

    De Zerbi spent much of the first half telling his back four to get higher up the pitch and it was perhaps understandable that captain for the day Archie Gray, Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi and Andy Robertson looked like a group of strangers.

    This was the foursome’s first competitive game together, but De Zerbi will need his Tottenham players to get to know each other as fast as possible if they are to challenge for Europe this season or even finish in the top half of the table.

    Recent findings suggest that bergvall and Conor Gallagher were hooked at half-time, with Tottenham two goals behind and De Zerbi clearly unimpressed. But the Italian’s changes did not prompt an instant response. In fact, things got even worse.

    Once again, Sangaré was heavily involved. He produced a well-hit shot that Kinsky had to save. For the second time, the goalkeeper failed to push the ball out of trouble and Michael Kayode was able to score.

    It has been revealed that michael Kayode with a third for Brentford just three minutes into the second half! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/40kOIlV5MU.

    Former managers Mauricio Pochettino, José Mourinho, Antonio Conte and Ange Postecoglou will all be scratching their heads about Spurs’ change of strategy in the club’s first post-Levy summer.

    It was Postecoglou who publicly shared his belief that Spurs would never spend £100m on a player and yet, just over a year after his departure, the club splashed out exactly that on midfielder Tonali.

    Whereas Postecoglou and his predecessors often had to answer questions over Spurs’ perceived profligacy, De Zerbi has been able to tease fans with promises of “bomba” signings.

    Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of Brentford vs Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League, a London derby between the smart spenders and the big spenders.

    That is probably an unfair dichotomy, because Spurs’s squad has been crying out for investment, and that has certainly arrived this summer. The club’s new leadership team has overseen more than £300m worth of purchases.

    The arrival of Jean Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi, two of the league’s best progressive passers from centre-back, makes it clear that improving Spurs’s build up play is a priority for Roberto De Zerbi.

    According to recent reports, de Zerbi wants his teams to draw pressure from opponents and progress down the middle of the pitch with short passes, so it was imperative that Spurs upgraded in midfield. They have done just that by buying Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali, for a combined £185m.

    Spurs’s forward options remain much the same though, which could prove a drag in the season’s early weeks. Compared to Manchester United, Chelsea, and Liverpool, Spurs do not have the same firepower, but they should have more control and solidity this season.

    Brentford lost just three league games at home last season, and they were unfortunate not to qualify for Europe. A lighter workload offers Keith Andrews the chance to consolidate on an excellent first season as head coach, and perhaps overtake some of those clubs with continental commitments.

    Midfielder Mamadou Sangaré, signed for £39m from Lens, looks the pick of their summer business, tipped to be a £100m sale to one of the massive boys (which is an unromantic perspective on the transfer, but very much Brentford’s model).

    Asked about the Mali international, Andrews said: “He’s a very talented midfielder who can do lots of different aspects of that role.

    Industry observers note that “He’s a very focused, very determined and very ambitious young man. He’s very humble but equally as hungry to achieve impressive things. He’s certainly a player on an upward trajectory.”.

    Forwards Jadon Anthony and Callum Wilson are other arrivals, and Michael Kayode’s long throws will continue to be a serious weapon.

    In a recent development, not to be outdone, the Jets have also been a disaster. Here's a quick synopsis of how things have gone for the Jets. Back on Feb. 24, Aaron Glenn said he would call plays on defense because it's one of his superpowers.

    As it turns out, though, he might have been wrong, and play-calling might actually be his kryptonite.

    According to recent reports, aaron Glenn gave up play calling vs the #Bills — that’s really significant of him. Called it his “super power” this offseason. He wants to call the game. To step back and be willing to give it to someone else, for the betterment of the team, isn’t something a lot of coaches are willing… https://t.co/ivYq4cnBca.

    Aaron Glenn saw Josh Allen coming up on the schedule in Week 10 and noted "No thanks, I'm good. You're now in charge of calling play on defense, Brian.".

    Sources indicate that so we have the Jets' broken defense going up against a Chargers offense that can't move the ball on anyone. I mentioned this game feels like a disaster waiting to happen and that disaster might happen after the game. If the Jets lose here, the temperature on Aaron Glenn's hot seat will get so hot that I don't think the Fahrenheit scale can actually measure it. We might have to switch over to Celsius.

    Recent findings suggest that the Chargers stunned the Ravens on Monday night by rushing for a season-high 160 yards. Running the ball is literally the only thing the Chargers can do on offense, which might work in their favor here because the Jets can't stop the run.

    The Chargers went into Week 10 with ZERO wins, so I feel crazy even thinking this, but this team might actually win two games in a row.

    Never in my life did I think I would live long enough to see a Jaguars-Giants game get flexed into the 4:25 p.m. late afternoon slot, but that's exactly what happened here. This game was originally scheduled to kick off at 1 p.m. ET, but the NFL decided to move it to 4:25 p.m. ET, and we're celebrating that fact here at CBS Sports by sending "The NFL Today" crew to MetLife Stadium.

    The NFL Today is headed to MetLife! 🔥The show will be LIVE outside the stadium ahead of @Jaguars vs @Giants this Sunday 🍿 pic.twitter.com/Bv2zAZ1htI.

    If you're going to be at the game, please come dressed as your favorite CBS Sports studio analyst.

    The Giants have been a huge surprise this season, and that's mostly thanks to John Harbaugh, who is my early vote for coach of the year. Harbaugh has been forced to start THREE different quarterbacks this season, but he still has the Giants at 5-3-1 and on top of the NFC East.

    The biggest surprise is that the Giants have somehow made J.J. McCarthy look good. I was led to believe by the Vikings that McCarthy was a washed-up bust, but apparently they just didn't know how to use him. McCarthy is the chopsticks of NFL quarterbacks. I hate chopsticks because I'm incompetent and don't know how to use them, just like the Vikings didn't know how to use McCarthy. On the other hand, my wife is such an expert with chopsticks that if every utensil on earth disappeared tomorrow and we only had chopsticks left, she would be fine, just like the Giants will be fine with McCarthy running the show.

    McCarthy played well enough to win in Week 10 against the Commanders, and the Giants might have won if they had a kicker who could make field goals from the right hash.

    Sources indicate that all 6 of Dominic Zvada’s missed kicks this season have come from the right hash, including his 33-yard miss last night.The Giants have lined up on the left hash for every extra point, where Zvada is a perfect 16/16. https://t.co/D9YzxVSYyx pic.twitter.com/UHJa8av5EK.

    Zvada's inability to hit a kick from the right hash is like Zoolander not being able to turn left, except worse.

    Industry observers note that I watched zoolander today (kind of like idiocracy) and the main character DEREK zoolander. Cannot turn left. Where have i heard of a derek related to the direction left. pic.twitter.com/e8cUEOU8Ct.

    It has been revealed that although I think the Giants will keep this game close, this will be the first week that the Jaguars finally unveil their new defense. They made three trades before the deadline, acquiring DT Davon Godchaux, DT Jordan Davis and safety Jessie Bates III. The Jags decided to keep Davis and Bates on the bench in Week 10 so they would each get a "bye" week this year. Those two will make their debut on Sunday, and I have a feeling the new-look Jags' defense is going to cause some problems for the Giants.

    PICK: Jaguars 30-23 over Giants.

    Industry observers note that for the first time in four years, the NFL is playing a game in Mexico City. I went to Mexico City once, and I was totally blown away by the food. I mean, they had a Chili's and Burger King UNDER THE SAME ROOF.

    If you're looking for food in Mexico City, I highly recommend this place. Only place I know of where you can get the world's two best restaurants under one roof TOGETHER pic.twitter.com/G58xvmA5DS.

    Industry observers note that someone needs to make that happen in the United States. Mexico is light years ahead of us when it comes to combining fast food with fast casual dining under one roof.

    OK, I need to stop talking about Chili's and start focusing on what could be the best chess match of the 2026 season: Kyle Shanahan vs. Brian Flores.

    In a recent development, through the first 10 weeks, the 49ers have had one of the best offenses in the NFL this year: They rank first in yards per game (399.8) and second in points per game (31.2). No one has really been able to stop them. The 49ers are so good that the Cowboys' defense basically gave up on trying to stop them in Week 10.

    As for the Vikings, they have one of the best defenses in the NFL. They've given up the fewest points per game (14) and the second-fewest yards per game (273.3). One big reason they're so successful is that they've gotten really good at destroying the opposing quarterback. The Vikings have racked up 37 sacks this year, which leads the NFL, and Flores loves to blitz on nearly every single play.

    The problem with that strategy is that Brock Purdy is basically the one quarterback you do NOT want to blitz.

    Leaders in EPA per drop back vs the blitz…DO NOT blitz these guys pic.twitter.com/Vn67jHblTm.

    It has been revealed that purdy thinks fast and gets rid of the football promptly. It's like he was designed in a lab to beat the blitz, but Flores is almost certainly aware of this, which means we'll probably see him cook up something special for the 49ers quarterback on Sunday. And now that we're talking about cooking, I'm thinking of Chili's again. I might need to take a lunch break.

    It has been revealed that I actually think the X-factor in this game is going to be the altitude. Mexico City sits at an elevation of nearly 7,400 feet, which is more than 2,000 feet higher than Denver. When you're playing at an altitude this high, it's not easy to get acclimated, which is why the 49ers will be spending the entire week in Colorado Springs, a city that has an altitude of just over 6,000 feet.

    Sources indicate that #49ers are set to travel to Colorado Springs tonight to begin altitude acclimation. They’ll have a normal practice week before traveling to Mexico City on Saturday to play the Vikings on Sunday night.

    On the other hand, the Vikings will be practicing at their normal practice facility, which has an altitude of 945 feet. Advantage, 49ers.

    This feels like a game where the altitude starts to get to the Vikings in the second half and that's when the 49ers will take over.

    It has been revealed that this is the final international game of the 2026 season, and I feel like the NFL should add some spice to the last international game each year by having the government revoke the losing team's passports. I'm not sure if that's legal, but I would definitely watch a reality show that consisted only of NFL players trying to get back home after having their passports revoked in a foreign country. It would be more entertaining than "The Bachelor.".

    Dan Quinn is probably going to be having nightmares all week and that's because he has to figure out a way to stop Joe Burrow, which is something that no one else has been able figure how to do this year.

    At this point, you've probably seen plenty of Burrow highlights this year, but if you're wondering just how dominant he's been, let me break it down for you:.

    Sources indicate that to put his yardage number in perspective, no other QB is even averaging 285 yards per game. He has five more TD passes than the next closest player and his completion percentage is so high that he might actually break the NFL single-season record of 74.4%, which was set by Drew Brees in 2019.

    Burrow is playing at an insanely high level, and now, he gets to face a Commanders defense that has given up the most passing yards per game in the NFC this year and second-most in the NFL (244.8). Burrow against this defense would be like inviting Joey Chestnut to your family's Thanksgiving and telling him to eat whatever he wants. You know you're going to get a Hall of Fame performance.

    Sam Darnold threw for 379 yards against this Commanders defense. Jameis Winston threw for 326 yards against this defense. J.J. McCarthy threw for 293 yards against this defense. I think what I'm trying to say here is that the NFL might want to invite Norm Van Brocklin's family to this game, because Burrow might take down his all-time single-game passing record of 554 yards.

    Recent findings suggest that although I feel like Burrow is going to have a substantial game, I think the Commanders' offense could also have some success. This is a home primetime game; Washington will be desperate, and Jayden Daniels has been playing well over the past few weeks.

    The last time these two teams played back in 2024, there wasn't a single punt in the game. That might happen again on Monday night because Zac Taylor doesn't sound like a guy who plans on punting this week.

    Asked what he didn't like about last night's blowout win against the Steelers, #Bengals coach Zac Taylor said, "We punted.".

    I'm going to say Burrow continues his MVP campaign by leading the Bengals to a shootout win in Washington.

    PICK: Bengals 34-27 over Commanders.

    Industry observers note that best pick: Commanders over Giants. Last week, I predicted that the Commanders would score exactly 24 in a win over the Giants, and guess what happened? Washington decided to distract the Giants by posting thirst traps of Hartman on social media and it clearly worked.

    Hartman is going to go down as the greatest practice squad signing in NFL history.

    In a recent development, worst pick: Texans over Browns. At the rate things are going, I might have to eliminate the "worst pick" section because I'm not getting any picks wrong. Over the past two weeks, I've gone 25-4 straight-up. The hilarious part is that I'm 0-2 when it comes to picking Browns' games and 25-2 in all other games.     #15423. Six lessons learned from Week 10: Brock Purdy belongs in MVP race, John Harbaugh makes more poor decisions

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1823 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Six lessons learned from Week 10: Brock Purdy belongs in MVP race, John Harbaugh makes more poor decisions

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1823 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • And on the 65th day of the NFL season, everyone finally had a win.
    • Industry observers note that also smiling?
    • Sources indicate that over in the NFC, there's a brutal battle.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    And on the 65th day of the NFL season, everyone finally had a win. The Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens wasn't the prettiest football, but the Chargers will find it as beautiful as any. A long flight home after a win feels a little shorter, and in a season that can't end soon enough, Jim Harbaugh and co., at least for one day, have something to smile about.

    Industry observers note that also smiling? The Browns, who watched all of their closest competitors for the final AFC wild card berth fall by the wayside. The only teams within two games -- the Patriots, Raiders and Ravens -- all lost in Week 10 while playing a quarterback who wasn't the Week 1 starter. Add in that the Browns got a crucial win over the Texans, and the AFC playoff picture looks pretty clear.

    Sources indicate that over in the NFC, there's a brutal battle. There are nine teams with winning records. The 6-4 Packers hold the No. 7 seed right now, but after a blowout loss to the Vikings, Green Bay finds the Seahawks and Rams -- also 6-4 -- right there. Lots can and will change, but the next time we see the Rams and the Packers facing off on Thanksgiving Eve, it will be arguably the most vital game of the year to date.

    As the NFC playoff hopefuls scratch and claw, though, they're all looking up at one team, led by one very, very good quarterback.

    Industry observers note that so much of Brock Purdy's success gets dismissed as him being a cog in the Kyle Shanahan system. And maybe there were times, earlier in his career, when that was closer to the truth.

    It is no longer remotely close to the truth. Yes, Shanahan set up some easy release valves for Purdy in the 49ers' 46-40 win over the Cowboys, like getting Christian McCaffrey matched up against Von Miller for the game-winning touchdown (I wrote about Shanahan deserving Coach of the Year on Sunday), but Purdy was truly magnificent. And he has been pretty much all year.

    One play exemplifying this was McCaffrey's first touchdown, when Purdy bought time and, at the last second, found McCaffrey. McCaffrey had been blocking in pass protection just a moment earlier.

    BROCK TO CMC OH MYSFvsDAL on FOX/FOX OneStream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/JoKDvzWC3K.

    The quick feet in the pocket. The full-sprint escape. The pump fake. The stop. The vision. The throw. This is elite quarterbacking.

    Recent findings suggest that purdy had several impressive plays like this one, including a 23-yard completion to Keenan Allen on third-and-12 after getting turned around 180 degrees while escaping a sack. This is what has separated Purdy from previous Shanahan quarterbacks: the creativity and out-of-structure playmaking. Purdy's 0.15 EPA per dropback on throws that take 3.5 seconds or more to come out is second, only to Joe Burrow.

    It has been revealed that speaking of Burrow, Purdy won't win MVP, it seems, because Burrow is on a historic heater. He's now a -115 favorite, per DraftKings. Josh Allen is second at +350, followed by Purdy at +425.

    But what Purdy, who has never finished above fourth in MVP voting, is doing with an ever-changing carousel of wide receivers is MVP-level stuff. The film matches the numbers, too.

    It has been revealed that next up? The Vikings -- a huge chance for Purdy to boost his MVP stock. Speaking of Minnesota ...

    It has been revealed that we're not just talking about "it looks better," which it absolutely does. We're talking about how Kirk Cousins changes how it looks, as in simply watching the unit moves before the action even happens.

    Under-center, play-action snaps per game.

    Average time to throw (seconds).

    In a recent development, this is why Minnesota got Cousins in the first place. He does everything Kevin O'Connell wants. He's happy to go under center, hit his back foot and let it rip. He doesn't quite rip it as hard as he once did, but the comfort in the system is evident. In fact, one of his most impressive snaps was him getting through audibles to set up a successful screen pass on third and 12.

    In a recent development, excellent work from Kirk Cousins pre-snap.All game, the Vikings were trying to take advantage of the numbers game with screen passes. They got a 4x2 advantage, and pulled the OL to keep the numbers on the outside pic.twitter.com/rXVHc17XDh.

    Remember, this is five days after he was traded!

    The Vikings look very different with Cousins, but Cousins looks very different from the last time he was with the Vikings, too. This was the same field on which he tore his Achilles in 2023, when he was playing some of the best football of his career. He had a rough two seasons in Atlanta and a resurgent half-season in Las Vegas. His movement (he even had two scrambles!) looks so much better than it did in 2024 and 2025. Hearing him after the game was a really cool moment, proving that he not only looks at home, but is, in a broader sense, home.

    An emotional Kirk Cousins, in his return to the Vikings at Lambeau Field: “I tore my Achilles here and it’s been a tough three years…” pic.twitter.com/8PhbEVs7Oq.

    Sources indicate that the Bengals have long had great wide receivers in Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, and we know how good a healthy Burrow is. But after Sunday night's dismantling of the Steelers, we need to talk about how good this offensive line is, too.

    Cincinnati's offensive line stonewalled what's supposed to be a strong Pittsburgh pass rush. Burrow was pressured on just 20.5% of his dropbacks, his lowest rate in over two years. T.J. Watt and Alex Highsmith combined for 63 pass-rush snaps ... and ZERO pressures. It's the first time ever both players have been shut out in the same game.

    It's a distant memory now, but the Bengals came into this year wanting to do more under-center stuff to help the run game and the offensive line. But the running game hasn't materialized, and the offensive line simply doesn't need the help of under-center and/or play-action concepts.

    Industry observers note that the Bengals are fifth in PFF's pass-blocking grade this year. They were 26th last year and 29th the year before that. What a huge jump, and in a great year to have one, too.

    According to recent reports, going back to where the week started. The Giants bungled a chance to get closer to putting this division away. Yes, give the Commanders credit where credit is due, but John Harbaugh was a huge part of Latest York's collapse.

    In a recent development, there are two conservative choices Harbaugh made late in the fourth quarter that stand out. The first was fourth-and-1 at the Giants' own 11-yard line with 3:26 left.

    According to recent reports, yes, their OWN 11-yard line. And, yes, they should've gone for it. This is reminiscent of the Lions going for it in nearly the exact same scenario in Week 7, which I wrote about back then. As Dan Campbell explained, he 1) thought his team would convert and 2) knew if it didn't, it would almost certainly get the ball back with a decent chunk of time left. The Lions failed, but Green Bay missed a kick, and the Lions ran the clock out.

    The same applied here, and Jameis Winston has been really good at quarterback sneaks, too, the previous play notwithstanding.

    It has been revealed that instead, Winston barked out his now-infamous "Who let the dogs out?" cadence, and the Giants took a delay-of-game penalty and punted. According to Ben Baldwin's fourth-down decision bot, 101 out of 101 models favored the Giants going for it.

    If you listen to nothing else today, at least listen to Jameis Winston's hard count here lmao 😂 pic.twitter.com/F1nr26EN3W.

    Sources indicate that after a Jayden Daniels interception, the Giants again played it safe with three straight runs, including a designed J.J. McCarthy run on third and 3. Sonny Styles sniffed it out for a 2-yard loss; the Commanders had been all over McCarthy's designed runs. Models were split on the fourth-and-5 decision; the Giants punted again, and to make matters worse, Jordan Stout shanked the punt 12 yards. Daniels led the game-winning touchdown drive, and Washington now has life.

    Overall, Harbaugh's conservative decisions -- he had another one in the fourth quarter and one in the first quarter, too -- cost Newly introduced York about 11.4% win probability, per Baldwin's bot. That's rough. If New York doesn't make the postseason, Winton's silly cadence will re-emerge for all the wrong reasons.

    Fernando Mendoza's first career was the top headline for what ended up being a 21-13 Raiders loss to the Seahawks, but Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald, special teams coordinator Jay Harbaugh and wide receiver Tory Horton teamed up for one of the smartest plays you'll see.

    The effort by the Seahawks special teams to prevent the touchback and keep the clock running 👏SEAvsLV on CBS/Paramount+Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/YF6eTRh4gs.

    '"Nine yards, 11 inches (into the end zone) -- literally, if there's any way to return the ball, return the ball,'" Harbaugh told his kickoff-return team. 'Burning the two-minute (warning on the kickoff return) is so impactful at that time.'".

    Harbaugh even reminded his unit of that right before it went onto the field, and then Horton defied gravity to do exactly what Harbaugh had asked.

    I love how Macdonald celebrated with Horton. The term "player's coach" is overrated and overused, but Macdonald clearly gets it. So, too does his staff and his team. And for those wondering about "illegal batting," it would have been a 10-yard penalty and a re-kick, which would have occurred within two minutes. Las Vegas obviously declined.

    We've seen so many clock mismanagements, especially on special teams, this season. Getting little details like this right is a sign of a coaching staff and team that's 100% bought in. We'd expect nothing less from the reigning champs.

    There have been 21 games decided by 15+ points over the past three weeks. In the seven weeks before that, there were only 26.

    We're starting to see the effects of the massive wave of quarterback injuries. The Patriots and Jets both lost their starters during Week 10, and the Cardinals are now on their third quarterback of the year. They accounted for three of the seven losses by 15+ this week. (Steelers, Titans, Packers and Falcons, you have no excuses).

    This might be the way it is going forward, too. The Colts and the Dolphins played one another in Week 10, but they project as two of the league's worst teams, and they play the Texans and the Bills, respectively, in Week 11. The Cardinals face the Chiefs. Unfortunately, there are just a lot of teams playing out the string already.

    'I feel betrayed, misled, in shock. It was a stupid thing for them to do': ANDY WOODMAN relives the moment he was 'brutally' sacked by Bromley - and how his best mate Sir Gareth Southgate helped him cope

    📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1468 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Published: 21:00 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 05:29 EST, 11 November 2026.
    • Every sacked manager has a sob story – but few dismissals have felt as harsh as Bromley’s recent decision to part ways with Andy Woodman.
    • It has been revealed that pound for pound, no club has outperformed their history, budget and expectations in English football across the last decade as much as Bromley.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By LEWIS STEELE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

    Published: 21:00 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 05:29 EST, 11 November 2026.

    Every sacked manager has a sob story – but few dismissals have felt as harsh as Bromley’s recent decision to part ways with Andy Woodman.

    It has been revealed that pound for pound, no club has outperformed their history, budget and expectations in English football across the last decade as much as Bromley. But after an understandably tricky start in League One – two wins from their first 10 games – Woodman was shown the door.

    In his first interview since that decision last month, the 55-year-old tells Daily Mail Sport about feelings of 'betrayal' and 'shock' before making his pitch to future employers. But the most eye-opening part of our candid conversation comes when I ask the man with more than four decades of experience to recall the club he took over in 2021.

    ‘Look, Bromley is your classic non-League club,’ says Woodman. ‘I mean that with the greatest respect to all non-League clubs and I hate the word “non-League” as I think it should be “League Three”, as they are all professional.

    Industry observers note that ‘But the facilities are non-League, the mentality is non-League. Everything is done day-to-day, hand-to-mouth, every penny counts, every decision that costs money counts, it is run by people’s personal money.

    ‘It was tough when I started: we had no turnstiles, no club shop, we trained on the pitch because it was astroturf, we had no gym.’.

    Andy Woodman was sacked as Bromley boss last month despite leading the club to the FA Trophy in 2022, promotion to the Football League in 2024 and then another promotion to League One last season.

    Recent findings suggest that woodman with the FA Trophy in 2022. 'Every manager who gets sacked, we all have a story of hardship to tell and all feel it is unfair,' says the former Bromley boss.

    Industry observers note that under chairman Robin Stanton-Gleaves, Woodman and Co, Bromley changed this mentality and shot up the pyramid, winning the FA Trophy in 2022, promotion to the Football League in 2024 and then another promotion to League One last season. Two months later, it was all over.

    Asked how he feels about the decision, Woodman, who used to coach in the Arsenal academy system, says: ‘Yeah, I feel betrayed. Every manager who gets sacked, we all have a story of hardship to tell and all feel it is unfair. That’s fine, I get how the football business works.

    ‘But the bit that didn't sit comfortably with me was the conversations I was having with people at the club or owners, everyone above me… there was no inkling of any of this. I feel misled. I was surprised.

    It has been revealed that ‘One day, we were talking about plans and the way forward and how to get through this sticky little period with players out injured, then the next minute it was a change of direction. Nothing like, “Right, you’ve got three games to turn it round”, none of that, nothing.

    Industry observers note that ‘My record was good there, the owner always noted if anyone can churn out results it was myself. Football has no patience. In football, people always forget where they come from. I understand wanting to move forward. It’s disappointing really, that’s the best word I can use. I feel let down.

    ‘It was just a normal day when they told me. I was going into training, popped across to where the chairman’s office was and then was just told, “We are going to take a change of direction”. It was no more than that, I didn’t try to change the decision or ask why.

    According to recent reports, ‘It was a two-minute conversation, it didn’t need more than that really. I went to tell the staff and went home! It sounds brutal and it is… I am sure people will read this and think, “You deserve this” and “You deserve that” but what else can you do? There’s no easy way of doing it.

    Sources indicate that 'When you have been told you are sacked, you don’t really want to stick around and have a long conversation. They didn’t give an explanation. They needed results, they noted. We lost to Leicester which was not a great result, obviously. But realistically they are Leicester… and we are Bromley.’.

    Recent findings suggest that 'It was a two-minute conversation, it didn’t need more than that really. I went to tell the staff and went home! It sounds brutal and it is'.

    Woodman, who used to be the Arsenal youth team goalkeeping coach, says: 'When I left Bromley that day, I just felt in shock to be really honest'.

    Industry observers note that to hammer home that last point: Woodman’s first game was against Wealdstone in April 2021 in the National League at Hayes Lane. On that same weekend, Leicester were hosting soon-to-be champions Manchester City. Oh, and the Foxes won the FA Cup a month later.

    Recent findings suggest that ‘When I left that day, I just felt in shock to be honest,’ continues Woodman. ‘I felt the next three games were winnable. I had played seven of the top 10 teams, beaten the top team Huddersfield, my goalie was just coming back from injury and some others were coming back.

    ‘We had two teams in the bottom four and one just outside so I felt it was my best opportunity to get some much-needed results.

    ‘To take someone out who has been in football 40 years and been in coaching 25 years and then to put (his former assistant) Byron Webster in charge who had just been fresh out of playing and has never done a coaching session… with every respect, it feels unfair to him. It was a stupid thing to do. I found that really strange, they took one point from those three games. It fascinates me.’.

    Now, with Bromley bottom of League One, Karl Robinson, the former Salford and MK Dons boss, has taken over. Woodman, though, is keen not to sound bitter and will remember his five-and-a-half years at the club with fondness. He states his best memories are taking Bromley into the Football League, playing at Newcastle in the FA Cup and beating ‘Hollywood Netflix club Wrexham’ in the FA Trophy final.

    It has been revealed that sir Gareth Southgate remains his best friend, the pair having met as teenagers in the Crystal Palace academy. They took turns in being best man at each other’s wedding and Southgate is godfather of goalkeeper Andy’s son Freddie, who is on Liverpool’s books.

    They also co-authored the 2004 book Woody and Nord which chronicles two polar opposite career paths that started at the same level, one going on to play (and later manage) England, the other a journeyman in the lower leagues.

    ‘Nothing surprises Gareth and I,’ adds Woodman. ‘We have been in the game for 40 years now. You can argue that in his tenure at England, he got them as high as they have ever been in 60 years and it still was not enough. So it doesn’t surprise us. People have to make decisions and they are business-related, only time will tell if it is the right decision but that’s not my problem any more.

    Woodman and lifelong friend Sir Gareth Southgate at the release of their 2004 book 'Woody and Nord' which charts two very different careers in football.

    Southgate is godfather to Woodman's son Freddie, a goalkeeper on Liverpool's books.

    ‘Gareth was very supportive, so was Alan Pardew and the support from the Premier League right down to the National League, there has been no end of messages I have had, which is comforting.

    According to recent reports, ‘That first Saturday after being out, I didn’t want to be watching or listening to the game, I just wanted to get away because that is the worst. I have had two clubs ring me, there are ongoing conversations and I am just making sure it is the right vehicle for me. What I mean by that is I want an owner that is aligned and who thinks they can compete to get out of their league.

    ‘My record speaks for itself. If you ask most managers how many promotions and trophies they have won, I bet over long careers, they haven’t got many. For me, with the smallest budget in the leagues, we maximised the team and maximised success.

    Recent findings suggest that ‘To get two promotions and an FA Trophy win against Wrexham, hitting the play-offs four times in five years, that is something I am really proud of. If nothing else, the Bromley supporters and town are grateful.’.

    #15421. Tech Report: NFL coaching hot-seat rankings: Cowboys' Brian Schottenheimer feeling even more heat

    Tech Report: NFL coaching hot-seat rankings: Cowboys' Brian Schottenheimer feeling even more heat

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2265 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • From 2018 through 2025, October featured at least one coach firing each season.
    • Sources indicate that the closer teams get to the end of the schedule, the more likely it is that someone will lose their job.
    • Schottenheimer's seat is hotter now than ever before.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    From 2018 through 2025, October featured at least one coach firing each season. That streak ended in 2026. Even the most embattled coaches made it to the campaign's third month. Heading into Week 11, the only major firing of the year has come at the executive level, with the Indianapolis Colts moving on from general manager Chris Ballard earlier in the season. But it is only a matter of time.

    Sources indicate that the closer teams get to the end of the schedule, the more likely it is that someone will lose their job. A cursory look at the standings sheds light on which teams are most likely to see changes in leadership, but not all losing records are created equal. For instance, the Las Vegas Raiders ought to feel optimistic about their future under first-year head coach Klint Kubiak, while the Dallas Cowboys are in a state of disarray with Brian Schottenheimer continually failing to field a competitive defense.

    Schottenheimer's seat is hotter now than ever before. His team just squandered an opportunity to inch closer to a playoff berth in one of the worst defensive performances in a home game in franchise history.

    Dallas' leader is far from alone on the hot seat. Here are the 10 coaches under the most pressure.

    A team that opened the year at 0-4 and is in an absolute fight to stay alive in the playoff race cannot afford to squander a 17-0 lead. Sunday's loss to the Cleveland Browns was about as disappointing of a defeat as any for the Houston Texans this season, and there have been some heartbreakers along the way, so that is saying something.

    Ryans took over the defensive play-calling duties after the first month of the year, and while the Texans are 3-2 with him orchestrating the unit again, the operation is far from fixed. Over the last three weeks, the defense gave up 27 points to a Deshaun Watson-led Browns team, 22 points to the Los Angeles Chargers and the worst offense in football and 27 points in a loss to J.J. McCarthy and the Latest York Giants. These are not exactly the most well-oiled operations that are moving the ball against Houston.

    In the month since New Orleans Saints owner Gayle Benson voiced her frustration with the team and called out coach Kellen Moore by name, the squad is 2-2 with a divisional loss to the Carolina Panthers. Going .500 over four games might be enough to win the NFC South in another down year for the division, but is it really a strong enough product to justify running things back in 2026? It probably will be if the Saints clinch a postseason berth.

    The final five weeks of the regular season feature all NFC South games and an extremely winnable home date with the Arizona Cardinals, so there is the potential for a strong finish to the year and a run to the division title. But things will probably get worse before they get better. Back-to-back road games against the Chicago Bears and Cincinnati Bengals, and the matchup against the Green Bay Packers that follows, could be disasters for a defense that ranks tied for 24th in points allowed.

    If Benson were to make an in-season move, a three-game losing streak to those opponents might prompt it. But if not, how the Saints fare against their rivals in the final month will likely determine Moore's fate.

    Cam Ward just turned in two of the best performances of his career, so at least the Tennessee Titans have that going for them. Sustained improvement from the former No. 1 pick quarterback is the main goal for the Titans at this stage of the season now that they are locked into the NFL's basement at 1-8 and have traded away their top defensive assets. Getting the absolute most out of Ward the rest of the way has to be Robert Saleh's top priority, because he probably will not have much else to show for himself.

    One-and-done coaches used to be a relative rarity in this league, but there has been one in each of the last five hiring cycles, and Saleh is the most likely candidate to add to that streak. If he can continue to squeeze promising games out of Ward and the other young weapons, including Carnell Tate (once he returns to the lineup), Saleh will have something to sell to the front office. If not, the Titans might be back in the market for another quarterback come draft time, and they will have to decide whether Saleh is the right person to oversee his development.

    Industry observers note that either the bye week came at an ideal time for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers to recharge their defense and ground game for the stretch run, or it will halt their momentum. Todd Bowles had better hope the former rings true, because he will continue to lean on those elements to save his job. There is a chance Baker Mayfield will be unavailable in Week 11 against the Detroit Lions, but it might not even matter at this point for the league's least productive passing offense. The Buccaneers will go as far as their rushing attack takes them.

    Sources indicate that bowles has the benefit of playing in the worst division in football. An 0-4 start and a 3-6 record at the bye would be crushing for most teams' playoff hopes, yet here are the Bucs -- just one game out of first place in the NFC South and with a win over the leaders under their belt.

    In a recent development, it is hard to trust a team that relies so heavily on forcing turnovers to string together wins, because takeaways are so unpredictable. The minute their fortunes turn and they stop turning teams over four times a game, this could go back downhill for the Buccaneers.

    There were no end-of-game snafus from Dan Quinn in Week 10, and what do you know; the Washington Commanders won a one-possession game. If he can stay out of his own way, he has the talent on his side with Jayden Daniels and a still-productive Stefon Diggs to win games like the 24-21 battle with the Fresh York Giants. Instead of clock management gaffes and head-scratching play calls, the Commanders dialed up a game-winning touchdown pass with 57 seconds left in a contest that put them right back in the NFC East conversation.

    Success has been fleeting for the Commanders this year, though. They have yet to win consecutive games and remain a game and a half under .500. As soon as they lose again -- an that could happen on "Monday Night Football" against the scalding-hot Bengals -- Quinn will be back under the microscope.

    Recent findings suggest that and as far as contending for the division and a playoff spot goes, Quinn has already used all but one of his opportunities against NFC East foes. He has to take care of business and hope for some help in the way of Giants and Cowboys losses in order to get into first place. And if he cannot do it this year when the division is wide open, will he ever?

    The first look at the post-trade-deadline Philadelphia Eagles comes in Week 11, when they host the Pittsburgh Steelers for an in-state rivalry game. A lost season could go even further down the drain in that spot, and the Eagles will likely be considerable underdogs the following week when they hit the road to face a Dallas Cowboys team that already beat them by 17. The next best opportunity for a win does not come until December, and the Eagles could be 2-9 by then. Now that they have committed to a rebuild, the question is less about whether this year is salvageable and more about how bad it will look when it is all said and done.

    It has been revealed that nick Sirianni earned all kinds of goodwill with his championship season in 2024, two trips to the Super Bowl and five consecutive playoff berths, but he also fell short of expectations last year and is at the helm for what may go down as the franchise's worst season of the century. In a "what have you done for me lately" league, the recent downturn may outweigh the heights of the Sirianni era when it comes time to decide whether he deserves to come back in 2026.

    He finally did it. Jim Harbaugh won a game in 2026. The threat of becoming the first 0-17 coach in NFL history is gone, but the stain of a brutal year will stick around on his otherwise prolific resume unless he is able to capture lightning in a bottle and rattle off a handful more wins between Week 11 and Week 18. Judging by the fact that it took a matchup against a Baltimore Ravens team that started its fourth different quarterback of the year -- one who had only been in town for less than a week -- to get victory No. 1 on the books, a sustained win streak is probably not in the cards for the Los Angeles Chargers.

    In a recent development, even though the run game got out of the mud and Omarion Hampton reemerged as a productive lead back in the win, the offense remains a massive problem and one that will probably continue to plague the franchise so long as Mike McDaniel is calling plays. Harbaugh retained him through the bye week and got a win out of that decision, so the offensive coordinator seems unlikely to go anywhere in the immediate future. A bigger question is whether the front office would give Harbaugh the chance to make an assistant change or if management would prefer to move on from Harbaugh himself.

    It has been revealed that offense will never be a problem for Brian Schottenheimer, but the defensive woes that plagued his first season and a half with the Cowboys just keep getting worse. At some point, Jerry Jones has to decide he cannot put up with the inexplicable lapses on that side of the ball, right? Some of that is his own doing and the result of his personnel moves, but a great deal of it falls on Schottenheimer and his assistants. It reached a new low in Week 10 -- one that might expedite the process of moving on from Schottenheimer and staff.

    Recent findings suggest that the porous unit wasted yet another gem from Dak Prescott, George Pickens and the offense by surrendering 46 points in the 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers. The scoring total marked the fourth-worst performance by the Cowboys defense in a home game in franchise history, and the 584 yards they gave up were the most ever at home. Christian McCaffrey gashed the defense for receiving touchdowns of 74 and 66 yards. Deebo Samuel made the Cowboys look foolish on a 70-yard scoring run on a reverse.

    In a recent development, the defense is undisciplined and uninspired and the main reason why Dallas is not in line to reach the playoffs. Sunday was a prime opportunity to capitalize on the Latest York Giants' latest loss and move within a game and a half of first place in the NFC East. Instead, the gap between the Cowboys and the top of the division looks insurmountable with the way this team keeps playing. That is an utter disappointment.

    It has been revealed that how poetic was it that mere days after the Indianapolis Colts completed their trade deadline fire sale, the remaining players in the locker room banded together for their first win since Oct. 4? Credit to Shane Steichen for motivating them enough to defeat the Miami Dolphins, because everything the front office did in firing general manager Chris Ballard and shipping many of the team's best players out of town indicated that they are punting on this season and looking ahead to the future.

    There is little reason to think this is more than just a one-week boost, though. Steichen is still a lame-duck coach now that his GM is gone, and he has fewer tools to work with than he did during the 2-7 start to the year. A difficult road ahead spells trouble. Do not forget, too, that the win they just pulled off came at home by a mere two points against a lowly Dolphins team that was without its starting quarterback. Two months from now, the Colts might look back at that win as their last of the season.

    Industry observers note that defensive play-calling is Aaron Glenn's self-proclaimed superpower. He touted the Fresh York Jets' potential on that side of the ball when he took over the duties at the start of the year. But after just half the season, his powers ran out. Glenn said on Monday that he ceded the play-calling role to defensive coordinator Brian Duker in last week's 31-12 loss to the Buffalo Bills.

    In a recent development, in essence, Glenn benched himself. It was a deserved move considering the Jets have the ninth-worst defense in EPA per play allowed and entered Week 10 having surrendered at least 26 points in each of their previous four games -- all of them losses. But if a coach with a so-called superpower cannot fix the defense, then why would a change in play-callers get the job done? It is a desperation move for a coach running out of answers and, frankly, running out of time.

    The 20-year-old sustained an ankle sprain during Algeria's 1-0 victory over Togo on Saturday, ruling him out of Tuesday's return fixture.

    The federation provided no further details regarding the expected length of his absence or when he will return to Leverkusen.

    Leverkusen will be hoping Maza recovers in time for Saturday's Bundesliga clash with Paderborn.

    The attacking midfielder has enjoyed an impressive start to the season, racking up four goals and four assists in 14 appearances for the German side.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Published: 06:24 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 06:28 EST, 11 November 2026.
    • It was a scene straight out of Will Ferrell's Elf.
    • One of the world's finest defenders was taking instructions from a schoolboy.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Published: 06:24 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 06:28 EST, 11 November 2026.

    It was a scene straight out of Will Ferrell's Elf. In the middle of Arsenal's Under-21 team huddle stood William Saliba, all 6ft 4in of him, towering over his teenage team-mates as 17-year-old captain Marli Salmon delivered his pre-match rallying cry.

    One of the world's finest defenders was taking instructions from a schoolboy.

    For the hundreds of Arsenal supporters who had descended on Boreham Wood's Meadow Park on Sunday, it was an extraordinary sight. Four months after suffering a back injury in France's World Cup semi-final defeat by Spain, Saliba was finally back on a football pitch.

    According to recent reports, but his carefully managed 45-minute appearance in a 5-2 victory over Aston Villa's Under-21s marked the beginning of another challenge. Saliba must now win back a place in an Arsenal defence which, remarkably, has barely missed him.

    That is largely down to Ezri Konsa, the £55million summer signing from Aston Villa who has been so impressive in Saliba's absence that Mikel Arteta faces a genuine selection dilemma.

    Saliba and Gabriel have been Arsenal's established central defensive partnership since the opening day of the 2022-23 season. But Konsa, arguably Arsenal's outstanding defender this term, has made a compelling case to keep his place.

    William Saliba towered over his teenage team-mates and played 45 minutes on Sunday.

    His performance in the 1-0 victory at Liverpool, Arsenal's first win at Anfield in 14 years, was particularly impressive. He won every ground duel, made 14 defensive contributions and completed eight clearances, leading the match statistics in all three categories. Liverpool failed to register a shot on target.

    Industry observers note that it was precisely the sort of performance that has given Arteta something to think about. And the Arsenal manager is understood to have challenged Konsa to fight for his place rather than simply make way for the returning Frenchman.

    Industry observers note that there is another solution. Konsa can operate at right back, a position he has occupied for both Villa and England, including during the summer's World Cup. That would allow Arteta to restore the Saliba-Gabriel partnership without sacrificing a player who has become such an important part of Arsenal's defence. For now, however, there will be no rush.

    Recent findings suggest that saliba's injury history explains why Arsenal have been so careful. In 2022-23, another back problem kept him out for 97 days and contributed significantly to the collapse of a title challenge that had seen the club spend 248 days at the top of the Premier League.

    Arsenal have since finished runners-up again and finally claimed the title last summer, but the lessons of that earlier setback have not been forgotten.

    Leading back specialists were consulted over Saliba's latest injury before the club settled on a conservative rehabilitation programme, deliberately extending his recovery rather than risking another setback.

    According to recent reports, he returned to full first-team training last Tuesday, ahead of Arsenal's 2-1 victory over Slavia Prague, but Sunday's appearance represented his first competitive action since July. His absence from France's squad during the international break should allow Arsenal to continue building his fitness without interruption.

    And there was plenty to suggest that the long wait has done little to diminish his quality.

    The Frenchman is building up his fitness after four months on the sidelines.

    Saliba faces a tough test to try and break up the partnership formed by Gabriel and Ezri Konsa.

    Playing comfortably within himself, Saliba repeatedly strolled past opponents before threading passes through the Villa midfield. At times he ventured so far forward after set-pieces that supporters began joking about whether he fancied himself as a centre-forward.

    Even at half-pace, the gulf between a world-class defender and academy football was obvious.

    Yet it was Saliba's interaction with his young team-mates that provided some of the afternoon's most revealing moments.

    Throughout the first half he could be heard directing Salmon, shouting 'man on,' 'high, high' and 'well done, Marli' as he guided his teenage defensive partner through the game.

    When Arsenal scored their opening goal, Salmon initially stayed back rather than joining the celebrations. Saliba promptly ordered him forward to enjoy the moment.

    Marli Salmon, pictured laying a wreath for Remembrance Day, was the one barking out instructions and seeing Saliba (left) among the youngsters was an extraordinary sight.

    It was a small gesture but typical of the interest Saliba has taken in Arsenal's younger players during his rehabilitation.

    He is understood to have spent time asking about their families and offering advice about life in professional football.

    In a recent development, one particular message has been the importance of looking after their parents if they are fortunate enough to make a successful career in the game. The affection is clearly mutual.

    Children clamoured for autographs as Saliba arrived and departed, while Arsenal had prepared for the unusual attention surrounding an Under 21 fixture.

    Large QR codes directing spectators to the team line-up had been displayed around the ground and a member of the first-team security staff accompanied Saliba between the dressing room and the pitch.

    In a recent development, his afternoon was meticulously choreographed. At half-time, his work completed, he disappeared into the changing rooms before leaving through a side exit.

    Saliba made his comeback for Arsenal's Under 21 side after a long injury absence.

    In a recent development, the 45 minutes will have provided reassurance to Arteta and Arsenal's medical staff, as well as a memorable afternoon for the teenagers who shared the pitch with him. For Saliba, though, the real work is only beginning.

    It has been revealed that few would have imagined when he suffered his injury in July that he might return to find his place under threat. Konsa's performances have changed that calculation.

    In a recent development, arsenal have their defensive cornerstone back. Now Arteta must decide what to do with him.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Erling Haaland has unveiled a dramatic latest look after cutting off his trademark blond locks.

    The Manchester City striker revealed his new buzzcut hairstyle on Sunday morning ahead of his side’s Premier League opener at home to Bournemouth later in the day.

    Later in the episode, Haaland called a host of famous faces, including Oasis singer Noel Gallagher and former City manager Pep Guardiola, to get their opinions on his transformation.

    Industry observers note that pep Guardiola's reaction to Erling Haaland's fresh haircut. 😭😂📲 Watch: https://t.co/4KvxC9e5mx pic.twitter.com/QQBCKKpGkP.

    Haaland, 26, has not sported short hair since his time at Borussia Dortmund, where he played three seasons before joining City in 2022.

    Sources indicate that haaland removed his hairband during a 4-1 win over Arsenal in 2023 on a raucous night at the Etihad as City beat their title rivals to move one step closer to winning the league. There will be no need for one now, though, with a close-cut look to mark a fresh campaign.

    It is a upcoming-look City in more ways than one this term with head coach Enzo Maresca looking to kickstart a new era following Pep Guardiola’s exit.

    Maresca is hoping for an immediate return to form in City’s Premier League opener after a chastening 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in the Community Shield last week.

    Recent findings suggest that so far, only Elliot Anderson has arrived but Maresca is hopeful the club will be active in the transfer market. Rodri has left for Barcelona while Savinho is closing in on a move to Tottenham.

    In a recent development, “I’ll try to find a new Rodri – it is what it is,” the former Chelsea manager stated. “Rodri, before he arrived here, he didn’t win the Ballon d’Or, he didn’t win the Champions League, he didn’t win the Club World Cup. Then he joined the club and then after he achieved many important things. Now the target for us is to try to find the new Rodri.

    In a recent development, “When David Silva was here, everyone was worried - Kevin [De Bruyne] arrived. When Sergio Agüero was here, everyone was worried – Erling [Haaland] arrived. When Ferdinando left, Rodri arrived. It’s just about this.

    Sources indicate that “When they leave, you need to be good and recruit the next one. They are all similar – David, Kevin, Fernandinho, Rodri, Agüero, Erling. It’s just normal, it’s a change. It’s not a problem, just go again and try to do the right things.”.

    Maresca added: “Hopefully we can do the things that we need to do. It doesn’t help that there are players that for different reasons want to leave, this is for sure.

    “But we need to adapt and we don’t want to keep players here that don’t want to stay.

    “The normal thing in transfer windows is that you have to wait because all the clubs try to keep players until the last week and then sell for more money.

    “It’s normal, I’m not worried about that. When the transfer window closes and we have all the squad there, for sure it will be different.”.

    #15412. Enzo Maresca tinkers his way to nervy Man City win

    📅 23 Aug 2026 • ⏱️ 26m • 📚 Deep Dive (5207 w)
    📖 Baca
    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

    Enzo Maresca tinkers his way to nervy Man City win

    📅 23 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 26 min read (5207 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~26 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning.
    • In a recent development, the narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image.
    • According to recent reports, all of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning. Enzo Maresca’s City started their Premier League season with a win, in the end, but three points masked the scale of the job he faces.

    In a recent development, the narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image. That macro reading overlooks the number of distinct issues with City that Maresca must fix. A upcoming midfield has to be recruited then blooded, a jittery defence needs settling down, and Phil Foden clearly requires help to recover the form which made him Premier League player of the year as recently as 2024.

    According to recent reports, all of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff. Josko Gvardiol scored an injury-time winner after City had trailed for most of the match, much of it a sloppy slog for the home side, who went behind in the 26th minute. The introduction of Rayan Cherki for Nico O’Reilly revived some familiar attacking effusiveness.

    Recent findings suggest that A lesser-spotted VAR-aided double celebration capped a tense but ultimately joyful day for Maresca. Marc Guéhi equalised from Cherki’s well-taken corner in the final minutes, then the expanded Etihad Stadium rapturously celebrated Gvardiol’s apparent winner, only to see it flagged offside. Video assistant Paul Howard intervened to show Gvardiol was onside from Cherki’s pass, before City’s fans, players and staff shouted twice as loud for twice as long to salute a morale-boosting victory.

    Sources indicate that joško Gvardiol scores in stoppage time! 👊 pic.twitter.com/FrTrfIg3ur.

    Recent findings suggest that “It’s the perfect day to be honest,” Maresca noted, although he may wish to set his expectations slightly higher. The East Stand which faces the dugouts at the Etihad unfurled a banner before the game welcoming him back to Manchester after his spell as Guardiola’s assistant. “I was very pleased when the game started, to watch the banner at the other side, and I was pleased at the end because we gave them the joy of the three points.”.

    His team made a fluid and furious start to Premier League football, suffused with a desire to prove the Community Shield is just a jumped-up friendly. A newly streamlined short-haired Erling Haaland ran with impatience, Elliot Anderson was a sinewy presence in midfield, Foden pulled off a gorgeous flick which led to a shot by Rico Lewis, well saved by Djordje Petrovic.

    Maresca’s selection was surprising, with six defenders in his XI, some deployed unexpectedly. Guéhi partnered Anderson in defensive midfield, while their England team-mate O’Reilly was often just behind Haaland in a No 10 role. There was an air of destiny about one O’Reilly run down the left flank in the first half, cruising to the byline and crossing presentably. Haaland was well positioned in the middle, but utterly fluffed his lines. Samson similes on standby, although perhaps he too was short of full match fitness during his early-season visit from the Philistines?

    Momentum shifted after Haaland’s miss, and Bournemouth took the lead when an innocuous high ball flummoxed Abdukodir Khusanov and Rúben Dias. They both pursued it, neither could make decisive contact and it left Evanilson on the ball with space to manufacture an unmissable cross for Marcus Tavernier.

    Marcus Tavernier fires Bournemouth ahead against Manchester City! 💥 pic.twitter.com/lSyNRfrTlc.

    Marco Rose, their upcoming manager, is facing a similarly daunting task to Maresca in living up to a predecessor who led Bournemouth to their highest-ever league finish and European football. “How the game went, it was quite unlucky to lose,” he remarked. “We had two situations, one corner kick and one attacking when we defended too passive, and that’s why we lost.”.

    His team showed an appealing coiled-spring quality after weathering the early City onslaught. They have players of class with the ever lively Tavernier, fresh signing António Silva seamlessly replacing Marcos Senesi at centre-back and silky Alex Scott, the Guernsey Grealish, whose current standing has now overtaken the man who gave him his nickname.

    They could not hang on here though, with Guéhi atoning for a free header planted wide with his day-saving equaliser. Cherki’s corner was nodded in from around the six-yard line then, with the game in the balance, the Frenchman provided another, thanks in part to the semi-automated gods smiling on Gvardiol and his fresh manager.
