    Recent findings suggest that tito Vilanova was addressing the world’s media in Camp Nou. For Barcelona in 2012, read Manchester in 2026. Enzo Maresca would be wise to study the manual for standing on the shoulder of a giant.

    Charged with maintaining the standards of a two-time Champions League-winning team many still consider the best ever, Vilanova’s substantial idea was effectively to leave the existing one alone, mastering the art of the subtle tweak.

    Describing the transition as seamless barely does justice to the changeover; Vilanova’s Barcelona side won 23 of their first 25 La Liga matches, snatching back the title lost to Real Madrid in Guardiola’s farewell campaign. Tragically, the promise of further honours to build on sturdy foundations was realised by others as Vilanova died from cancer in 2014.

    After a brief stint by Gerardo Martino, Luis Enrique gave the dream team of Lionel Messi, Andrés Iniesta and Sergio Busquets further La Liga titles and another Champions League win.

    The so-called “impossible job” of being bound by the weight of the preceding genius, therefore, was no such thing.

Belgian goalkeeper Marco Bizot starts and there is also a place for teenager George Hemmings. Emi Buendia in what looks like the central striker role. It is certainly a bracing opening day to the season for Unai Emery.

    In a recent development, welcome to live coverage of Sunday afternoon’s 2pm Premier League kick-offs. Enzo Maresca faces the unenviable task of following Pep Guardiola’s decade of dominance at Manchester City and his reign begins in earnest with a visit from Bournemouth, who themselves are ushering in a newly introduced era after Marco Rose succeeded Andoni Iraola. A bruising 3-0 defeat in the Community Shield last weekend does not bode well for City’s hopes of closing the gap to Arsenal, but Maresca will be telling his charges that this afternoon is a fresh start: a new week and a new competition, plus Erling Haaland has a new haircut….

    The Italian’s squad has been shorn of World Cup winner Rodri, who departed for Barcelona this week, and the spotlight will turn to £116m club-record signing Elliot Anderson who is expected to make his Premier League debut with City. Jérémy Doku is out for two to three weeks after suffering a calf injury, which could open the door for Jack Grealish, with City bereft of wide options. City will have their work cut out as Bournemouth, fresh off a historic sixth-place finish last season, look to extend their 18-match unbeaten run from the end of last season. The Cherries won three of their five pre-season matches, which included an eye-catching 10-1 victory over Serie A side Genoa.

    Brighton and Hove Albion welcome Aston Villa to the Amex for their 2026-27 season opener having travelled 220 miles north of the Arctic Circle to play Norwegian side Tromso in their Europa Conference league play-off on Thursday. Fabian Hurzeler’s side face the defending Europa League champions without Carlos Baleba, who is on the brink of joining Manchester United, as well as injured wingers Kaoru Mitoma and Yankuba Minteh. While Unai Emery has lost key players in Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Ezri Konsa and Lucas Digne, the funds raised has gone towards seven signings, with Zion Suzuki, the Japan goalkeeper, in line to make his first start for Villa.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Thomas Tuchel's England ended Spain's 43-game unbeaten run with a hard-fought 3-2 win at Metropolitano Stadium. FC Bayern's striker Harry Kane opened the scoring from the penalty-kick he won before the half-time break as the 33-year-old became the only player to net in all six League A group stage games of the UEFA Nations League.

    England were 3-0 ahead by the hour mark after goals from Arsenal defenders Ezri Konsa and Ben White, but Eliott Anderson's decision that led to a red card and a penalty for Spain changed the complexion of the game.

    Industry observers note that having won the penalty-kick that was converted by Mikel Oyarzabal, Lamine Yamal assisted substitute Nico Williams for the second goal with 15 minutes left to play. However, Bayer Leverkusen's Jarell Quansah and co. produced a defensive masterclass for the rest of the game to secure a top spot finish for England.

    Recent findings suggest that spain's unbeaten run ended with their last game of 2026 as the world champions suffered their first defeat since March 2024. Luis de la Fuente's side had to settle for a second-placed finish, with England having a better goal difference after avenging their defeat at Wembley by the same scoreline.

    In the other game from the group, Croatia beat Czechia 2-1 thanks to goals from former Bundesliga stars Ivan Perisic and Lovro Majer. Hoffenheim's attacker Adam Hložek scored the only goal for Czechia, who are relegated to League B after losing all six games in the group.

    • Perth Glory supporters have demanded action over a confrontation near HBF Park, with video posted on social media showing a group of young people as they crowded around a parked white vehicle and aggressively rocked it from side to side.

    By JOSH ALSTON, SPORTS REPORTER.

    Published: 03:01 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 07:38 EST, 11 November 2026.

    Shocking footage of soccer fans after a match has reignited complaints about public safety, following previous warnings repeated violence was putting families at risk.

    Perth Glory supporters have demanded action over a confrontation near HBF Park, with video posted on social media showing a group of young people as they crowded around a parked white vehicle and aggressively rocked it from side to side.

    Other footage filmed from across the road shows young people confronting fans in the street, with the group spread across the footpath and roadway outside nearby businesses.

    Images shared alongside the complaints show fighting on previous occasions, as well as damaged fences and other property. Supporters allege the material documents a recurring problem involving the same group and have demanded bans and stronger security measures.

    The footage prompted calls for bans and renewed criticism of matchday security, with supporters alleging genuine fans face strict enforcement over minor problems while more serious behaviour goes unchecked.

    'The same group of troublemakers causing chaos and mobbing random people', one fan posted on social media platform X.

    Young people crowd around a parked white car and aggressively rock it near HBF Park in footage that has sparked anger among Perth Glory supporters.

    Supporters allege genuine fans are being left feeling unsafe at Perth Glory matches.

    Tagging Perth Glory, they added: 'It's time you do something about it. People have had enough.'.

    The supporter also called for individuals to be banned and, in a subsequent post, alleged nearby property had been damaged.

    WA Police, Perth Glory and A-Leagues have all been contacted for comment.

    Perth-based football podcast and digital channel The Far Post Perth shared the original post, adding its own demand for intervention.

    'Not a good look at all and something needs to be done about the problem at this point, genuine supporters are being impacted,' the account wrote.

    One commenter alleged the group had been moving through the venue during the match while being followed by security and police.

    'This is the mob that was walking back and forth all game with security/police following,' they wrote.

    'We don't need this at HBF Park. It makes many people feel unsafe when these wannabe thugs just shove their way through.'.

    Another video reveals young people confronting fans on the street outside nearby businesses.

    Photographs of damaged fences and other property have fuelled calls for stronger action.

    The person who posted the footage claimed that 'after the game the police and security were nowhere to be seen'.

    They also shared a separate video from February, alleging it indicated an earlier confrontation involving the same group.

    The February post had complained about people attending matches in The Bay supporter area and allegedly fighting with other young spectators.

    The complaints follow a strongly worded statement issued last year by supporter groups The Bay Perth and Shed End Perth, which demanded sanctions after a separate incident outside Gate 2 during the second half of a match at HBF Park.

    The groups said they were aware of footage circulating online and distanced themselves from those involved, alleging physical confrontations had become a recurring problem.

    'We want to make it absolutely clear that those involved are not fans and do not represent our supporter groups, our values, or the wider football community,' their joint statement read.

    'These individuals consistently attend matches with the sole intention of causing problems rather than supporting the team, and their behaviour is completely unacceptable.'.

    The statement alleged confrontations had occurred in active supporter areas and the Eastern family stand, extending the groups' concerns beyond the stadium's most vocal sections.

    Images shared alongside the complaints show fighting on previous occasions.

    'In almost every single game, they have caused physical confrontations in both the Active areas, and in some cases the Eastern family stand too, and it is deeply frustrating that this behaviour continues without meaningful consequences,' the groups said.

    They alleged the behaviour was damaging the experience of supporters who attended matches to follow Perth Glory.

    The groups also accused matchday security provider NPB Security of failing to respond adequately to incidents.

    Their criticism included allegations that a rotating contingent of inexperienced security staff was being deployed and that personnel were unable or unwilling to intervene when serious problems arose.

    'The lack of accountability from NPB Security is unacceptable and has undermined the safety of the matchday environment,' the statement read.

    'Warnings and passive responses are clearly not working.'.

    The groups called for bans and other sanctions, warning that further incidents could affect spectators and people working at the ground.

    'Without firm action, including bans and real consequences, these so-called 'fans' will continue to put genuine supporters, families, and staff at risk.'.

    They urged the club and stadium authorities to identify those responsible and impose firm sanctions.

    Their earlier warning has been followed by fresh complaints about how security rules are enforced at Perth Glory matches.

    'Meanwhile security go OTT about bottled water in the shed or actual fans taking t-shirts off,' one supporter wrote in response to the latest footage.

    Another commenter similarly complained that removing a shirt in the supporter bay could result in ejection, while alleging people involved in violence escaped consequences.

    The Far Post Perth also challenged a response that dismissed the latest incident as 'kids being kids'.

    Sources indicate that 'Kids being kids is vandalising other people's property? Interesting,' the account replied, referring to the allegations of property damage.

    However, one person responding to the original footage questioned whether those shown in the street were Perth Glory supporters.

    Sources indicate that 'In the second video, the person filming is standing where the stadium is. These idiots look like they are walking from the other side of the road,' the commenter wrote.

    'Are we sure they are even Glory fans? Or just troublemakers.'.

    The person who uploaded the footage insisted they were, although the posts do not establish that the same individuals were involved in each of the incidents raised by commenters.

    The Bay Perth and Shed End Perth had made their position on violence explicit in their earlier appeal for action.

    'Violence, fighting, and antisocial behaviour have no place in football,' they remarked.

    'HBF Park, The Shed, The Bay and all areas of the ground should be a safe and welcoming environment for all supporters, families, players, and staff.'.

    Italy opened the score against Belgium in the other game from the group, but Marc van Bommel's men responded immediately as their substantial win sent them to the knockout stages.     Sources indicate that the sight of Bukayo Saka hobbling down the red carpet at the Ballon d'Or ceremony came as a surprise. Only those closest to him knew why he was there, and the years of toil that led to this moment.

    While his England team-mate Harry Kane claimed the night's top on-pitch prize, Saka – who had suffered a thigh injury just days before against Kane's Bayern Munich – was at the London Palladium to collect the Socrates Award for his humanitarian work.

    Joining a roll of honour that includes previous winners Vinicius Junior, Sadio Mane and Luis Enrique, Saka walked onto the stage, reached into his suit pocket and read a letter from a 14-year-old boy in Rwanda whose eyesight had been restored through his charity work.

    Now, Daily Mail Sport can reveal the scale of the Arsenal star's involvement over the last four years with the BigShoe charity, which funds operations, feeds children and helps with disaster relief across the world. From restoring the eyesight of that 14-year-old in Rwanda to helping provide life-saving procedures for 120 children in Nigeria, Saka's impact goes far beyond the stadiums he dazzles in.

    In a recent development, and this is no passive act of philanthropy. BigShoe president Valerie Fiesser's phone is often inundated with messages from Saka when the charity is delivering projects in poverty-stricken countries such as Nigeria and Rwanda. Many of the project ideas come from the 25-year-old himself.

    Sources indicate that 'Bukayo is really, really productive,' Fiesser tells Daily Mail Sport. 'He is really pushing how he wants to help. I think for him it is never fast enough to help. Sometimes Bukayo comes up with projects and he states, "Shouldn't we help here?" So he is really interested in it. It is not like he is just sending money and saying, "OK, nice, we'll do a project in Nigeria".

    Bukayo Saka was handed the Ballon d'Or Socrates Award for his humanitarian work last month.

    Saka has worked with BigShoe charity for years - helping those in poverty-stricken countries.

    In 2023, Saka donated 50 containers to help provide shelter for 255 people impacted by the devastating earthquake in Morocco.

    'When we are on the ground, he is texting, "Is everything alright? Is everybody safe? Are all the children safe? Which services do we have? Can I see pictures? Send me pictures, send me pictures, send me pictures!".

    Recent findings suggest that bigShoe, a German-based charity founded during the 2006 World Cup, began years ago by funding life-changing surgery for Nourisson, a young girl from Togo born with a cleft lip and palate. The Togo national team, playing at their first World Cup, were based in the city of Wangen im Allgau, which brought the story to prominence in Germany.

    The charity is now a worldwide network of football stars, fans and partners, with more than 10,000 children around the globe having benefitted via projects ranging from medical supplies to shelter and food. The organisation has also worked with Antonio Rudiger, Paul Pogba and Saka's ex-Arsenal team-mates Mesut Ozil and Oleksandr Zinchenko.

    Fiesser vividly remembers how Saka first got in touch, in early 2022.

    'He just really randomly wrote us an email,' she says. 'He asked us if we can help together in Nigeria after seeing a project of another soccer player. He said, "I want to help children, I want to help people and can we do something". (It was) really just random.'.

    That initial conversation promptly developed into a project in late 2022 which funded 120 life-changing medical operations for children in Nigeria. Some of the youngsters were suffering from brain tumours, while others required treatment for hernias.

    Sources indicate that 'This was an incredible project because it was the first project in Nigeria together with him,' she indicates. 'It was really life-changing for the children because some had a brain tumour, some had hernia problems.'.

    Saka has since helped support healthcare check-ups for more than 580 children in Rwanda and provide disaster relief after devastating earthquakes in Morocco and Turkey, while his involvement has extended far beyond financial backing.

    The charity is now a worldwide network of football stars, fans and partners, with more than 10,000 kids having benefitted via projects ranging from medical supplies to shelter and food.

    'We did a disaster relief where we provided homes for the earthquake victims in Morocco and Turkey and he was asking questions like, "Do they have electricity there?"' she notes.

    Sources indicate that 'He is really thinking, "Is it worth it, does it make sense to do this, or is it just putting the container and then the people do not have water and they cannot live there?" So he is really, really smart. And yes, I think he is an amazing human.

    'It was never about him. It was always about the children and how we can help. It was never like, "OK, we are talking to one of the best players of the world." I think he is raised like this. His family made him the man he is now.

    'I think he is raised like this, that you have to be a good human being and to help others and just have an impact in life.'.

    Saka and his family are directly involved in the projects, identifying communities in need and deciding exactly how support should be delivered. His mother, Adenike, is a key figure.

    In a recent development, 'We decide together where we can help, how we can help and then we actually help together,' Fiesser notes. 'Me and his mother WhatsApp, call regularly. She has played a big part and is a driving force.

    According to recent reports, 'Three months ago we renovated a school in Rwanda and we provided them with water filters for clean drinking water. We also built girls' changing rooms, a newly introduced soccer pitch and a new library. Bukayo's family was on the ground, twice.

    In a recent development, 'We decided after we saw that the families are really hungry in this area to do food packages. It is our next project in November and December.

    It has been revealed that 'He (Saka) really wants to make a difference. He wants to change lives.'.

    While Saka will continue to chase trophies in Arsenal red and England white, his greatest legacy may ultimately be measured in the lives he has changed far beyond the football pitch.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that it had to end that way, didn’t it? A last-minute goal, a sense of what might have been and a helter-skelter contest that will take days to decipher.

    Newcastle versus Liverpool became the Premier League’s most dramatic fixture when Kevin Keegan was manager here and, on the afternoon they flocked to the “cathedral on the hill” to pay tribute to the late, great superstar, we were treated to a contest that was in keeping with his narrative.

    Liverpool operating with the discipline of a basketball team undoubtedly helped, and we can examine those gaping chasms soon enough, but the poignancy of seeing Matthias Jaissle looking as bereft as Keegan at Anfield 30 years ago at the final whistle was impossible to ignore.

    Really, the German’s first match in charge of Newcastle should have ended with three points. His team are a work in progress – rich in youthful exuberance though prone to lapses – but how they fought, ran and worked to give the locals the result they wanted.

    They were almost at the finish line, seconds away from beating Liverpool here for the first time since December 2015, but then Lewis Hall ran into Victor Muñoz, sending the Spanish substitute sprawling, and Stuart Attwell pointed to the penalty spot. Dominik Szoboszlai inflicted maximum damage.

    It has been revealed that dominik Szoboszlai equalises from the spot in the 99th minute! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/0Ag9WitqHt.

    “I have clear thoughts,” Jaissle noted quietly, as he was asked to reflect on the day-wrecking decision. “I guess you call it a soft penalty here. If you give it, you need to give a lot during this match and a lot during the season. I don’t know if it that is good for football.”.

    Here was the third time in four seasons Liverpool had scored in injury time in front of the Leazes Stand, after Darwin Núñez (2023) and Rio Ngumoha (2025), and their eighth goal beyond the 90th minute in collisions with Newcastle is a Premier League record against the same opponents.

    No wonder he was stunned. Jaissle had spent idle moments in the build-up thinking about what might happen if Newcastle scored an early goal and, much to his delight, fantasy became reality in the most thrilling fashion. On this emotional afternoon, it was fitting the hosts scored first.

    One of Keegan’s great early wins as Newcastle manager was in November 1993, when his team blew away Liverpool in the snow and Andy Cole scored a first-half hat-trick. His first goal that day came after five minutes and, by happy coincidence, the clock stopped at that moment for Anthony Elanga, too.

    How Liverpool went from having a chance of their own to conceding 20 seconds later is something Andoni Iraola will have to address rapidly, but that is what happened: Ryan Gravenberch should have shot, instead he passed and Amar Dedic intervened, his interception finding Will Osula.

    Off Osula galloped, Liverpool’s defenders looking leaden-footed as they gave pursuit, and he ushered Elanga into open space. Once he was in the clear, he was not for catching and his shot was perfectly placed beyond Alisson Becker.

    Industry observers note that an electric start! Anthony Elanga gives Newcastle the lead inside 5 minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/8DYYFJ9i6F.

    As Elanga was mobbed, the recriminations started. Fingers pointed at each other, Iraola spun around in dismay. Liverpool were easy to play against last season – Iraola’s Bournemouth had scored two identical goals against them on the opening day 12 months ago – and old habits die hard.

    According to recent reports, “We should finish the play,” Iraola conceded. “We created a great chance. We are on the edge of the box and have a clear opening to shoot and we decide not to. We don’t finish it properly and then you have to give credit to Elanga, who wins the race.”.

    What could Liverpool offer in response? The answer before the interval was nothing, other than a shot from Florian Wirtz that was well saved by Lukas Hornicek. The first half was wretched and it was difficult to see what had changed from the final throes of Arne Slot.

    Recent findings suggest that this, to be clear, is no criticism of Iraola, more a spotlight on players who need to step up. They did that momentarily in the second period, when Cody Gakpo equalised. He was afforded too much time by Newcastle’s defence but, still, his finish from 20 yards was super, zipping beyond Hornicek.

    Cody Gakpo with a fine finish to equalise for Liverpool! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/cfDQWbES2v.

    In a recent development, but parity was secured for less than two minutes before Newcastle scored a near-carbon-copy second goal, another counter-attack – this was one led by the outstanding Yoane Wissa – ending with substitute Joe Willock finding a corner of Alisson’s net. Again the inquests followed.

    Sources indicate that "Wow!"Joe Willock restores Newcastle's advantage almost instantly with an exceptional finish! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/8IKPUgqapK.

    Recent findings suggest that “We had the numbers to defend it better,” Iraola stated. “It’s not like they caught us by surprise, but we didn’t defend it properly. We should compete for the first ball and probably make a foul, be a little more aggressive as we had the numbers to defend it.

    “You don’t want to concede transitions and we’d been preparing them in the week for transitions.”.

    Why they didn’t follow the plan that had been set is something that Iraola must address, but he will be relieved that the days spent this week are not dissecting a defeat, as Wissa should have wrapped up the contest, only for Alisson to make a brilliant save to thwart the Congolese striker.

    It has been revealed that those missed chances should not have mattered but in the final throes, Hall misjudged the angle Muñoz attacked him from, he got his challenge wrong and, after a pause, Attwell pointed to the spot. Given the agony Liverpool have inflicted, the outcome was as clear as black and white.

    According to recent reports, “We scored at the end, so you have a better taste,” Iraola remarked. “Before the game, we wouldn’t have signed for this result. It’s a reward. It’s only a point, but at least it’s something that’s deserved.”.

    According to recent reports, plenty would contest his conclusion. Liverpool got away with it – and Iraola is about to find the hard work is only just beginning.

    A really soft one, if you give that, they’ll be more in the future, I’m not a fan of that.

    Their heads are a little down but we know we had many challenges, we’re in a huge transition phase at the moment.

    It has been revealed that it’s a brave project but I like the challenge, working with young lads, they were tired. Lewis Miley just came back from an injury but they did an amazing job and it’s just about getting adapted to the league.

    The crowd here is unbelievable and the quality. Every change can be decisive and it’s something I really enjoy. We’re clear in our approach and you can adjust in the game if you plan ahead.

    It’s not the result you want, but scoring in the last minute gives us a better feeling. I value that the players never gave up. I’m sure we had more chances, it’s unfair they’re winning very early and overall, I think we’ve had the better chances.

    We were probably in the first half not finishing anything, we had a lot of balls on the edge but we needed to shoot. We don’t finish play and then they win on the counter-attack.

    The players coming from the bench gave us energy and you can feel the way we want to play.

    Sources indicate that overall, we played a lot in their half and had good moments and phases on the ball. The first goal was more difficult to defend, Anthony Elanga is a fast player. The second, I think we had the numbers but sometimes you have to finish the play and try and win the ball.

    What a special club, what a special man, that’s why we gave him a significant credit. The fans were unbelievable today. I think we gave them so much back today and that’s what we need to give them all season.

    We know we needed to give the fans something after this period so that’s why we tried to start fast. The fans pushed us until the end.

    By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

    Published: 05:59 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 10:52 EST, 11 November 2026.

    Stan Collymore has paid an emotional and heartfelt tribute to talkSPORT presenter Danny Kelly after he passed away at the age of 69.

    Kelly had been undergoing treatment after being diagnosed with cancer of the oesophagus, which led to him stepping away from his talkSPORT role in March.

    In an enhancement to fans in August, Kelly informed fans his cancer treatment had 'definitely not gone to proposal' after revealing he had been hospitalised on seven occasions, including spending time in intensive care.

    On Wednesday morning, talkSPORT then heartbreakingly confirmed the legendary broadcaster's death in a statement.

    Kelly was known to be a mentor for many younger journalists and pundits, one of whom was former England, Liverpool and Nottingham Forest star Collymore.

    And, shortly after his tragic passing was confirmed, Collymore took to social media to pay his respects to Kelly and thank him for the role he had played in his life and career.

    talkSPORT presenter Danny Kelly has died at the age of 69, the broadcaster declared on Wednesday.

    Stan Collymore was one of many individuals to share an extremely heartfelt tribute to Kelly.

    Industry observers note that kelly had updated fans throughout his treatment, which he admitted in August had 'not gone to strategy'. Source: X/dannykellywords.

    'This morning I was told of the passing of my good friend and colleague, Danny Kelly,' he wrote. 'The tributes to him in the coming days from those who knew him and worked with him will give you an idea of how much he was loved.

    'I loved him too. Very much so. A man who I called "Dad" on air because I wished he was. I hope you give me a few minutes to read my thoughts, and I hope they do you justice, Dan.

    'By 2008 I was a mess. I would sleep 18 hours a day, the other 6 mostly wanting to die. Once or twice a week I would open my laptop, organise football tabs, gossip and news as prep for jobs in broadcasting that I knew would never come, "just in case". When hope dies, we die, after all.

    'Then Danny Kelly came into my life. I was driving out of London having been to see a psychiatrist about the state I was in and had BBC London on the radio. Danny was presenting with a guest, reviewing books. My name came up in the conversation, so I called in.

    Sources indicate that 'We hit it off straight away, talked about football for what seemed like forever but was probably a standard 10-12 minute section. But for me it sparked a temporary respite from sleep and chronic mental health issues and even for that I was grateful.'.

    Collymore continued: 'A couple of years later Danny joined talkSPORT to do the 7-10pm slot through the week. He told me he was offered a few co-presenters but he remembered that conversation we had and he wanted me to do it.

    Sources indicate that 'A lifeline of work, passionately talking about our sport, having fun and feeling a value as a human again. Something lost for 7 long years. Danny gifted me that. Without that I know I wouldn't be writing this today.'.

    Collymore went on to highlight some of Kelly's many qualities and provided further insight into their close relationship and how he was supported on his broadcasting journey.

    '"Always fresh, never frozen" was the tagline in a Domino's read we had to do in the show, something we'd instinctively greet each other with until our last meeting, in a pub, broadcasting for talkSPORT around 3 years ago,' he added. 'I didn't know that time would be the last, but perhaps fittingly we hugged as I left, I'm glad I did.

    'The highlights were loved. They were funny, honest, insightful and I hope, along with Saggers after that, proof that Danny's belief in me was worthy. But to say my love for him was only thanks for a job doesn't even scratch the surface.

    'His kindness, his phone calls late at night (Dan was a notorious night owl) of support, his man hugs, his indomitable spirit, his big brain on anything from football to music to geopolitics, his love, as I know many others will testify, came from the biggest of hearts and the biggest of souls housed in a giant of a man in every sense.

    Sources indicate that 'Dan, thank you, thank you for the kindness, the fun, the hope, the support and for being someone to look up to and aspire to be. I love you very much, I know I'll hug you again some day. Thank you for everything.

    '"I love football Stan, I love it ".'.

    Collymore was one of many to pay tribute to Kelly, with former talkSPORT Breakfast host Laura Woods also highlighting the role he had played in her career.

We had production meetings, sitting around Danny, it was like kids at school, great stories. The level of knowledge he had, about anything and everything.     'He would say it how it was, I loved that. I was in awe of him. He challenged me in the right way. He’d give you so much knowledge, I credit him with my early development. I will miss him.'.

Bundesliga’s most dangerous attacking sides.

    One of the encouraging aspects of Hertha’s attacking development has been the contribution of different players throughout the squad, having relied heavily on individuals in years gone by.

    Sebastian Grønning has provided an important focal point in the final third, while other members of the squad such as Oluwaseun Adewumi, Josip Brekalo and Mads Pedersen have also demonstrated their ability to contribute in attacking areas.

    Rather than depending entirely on one goalscorer, Hertha have demonstrated an ability to find contributions from different areas of the pitch.

    Industry observers note that their 5-3 victory over Eintracht Braunschweig provided an excellent example of that attacking depth. Despite falling two goals behind, Hertha responded with an impressive comeback, demonstrating their ability to create opportunities and punish opposition mistakes.

    Their 2-1 victory over Wolfsburg before the break was another significant result, with Adewumi and Deyovaisio Zeefuik finding the net in front of a packed Olympiastadion. Against one of their promotion rivals, Hertha highlighted they could translate their attacking quality into key points.

    The relationship between Hertha’s expected goals and actual goals scored is particularly interesting.

    Their 22.9 xGoals figure indicates that they have consistently created opportunities worth more than 22 expected goals, while their 25 goals demonstrate that they have also managed to convert those chances effectively.

    Although the difference suggests a degree of overperformance in front of goal, the gap is relatively modest compared to the overall volume of opportunities created.

    According to recent reports, this is important when assessing whether their current position is sustainable. Hertha are not simply benefiting from an unusually clinical spell; their underlying chance creation suggests they have the attacking foundations to remain competitive throughout the campaign.

    Ranking second for xGoals, joint-third for goals scored and sixth for shot efficiency, they are performing strongly across all three attacking indicators.

    For a club that has endured several frustrating years since dropping out of the Bundesliga in 2023, the current campaign represents a welcome change in fortunes.

    Hertha have not only produced the results required to reach the summit but have also developed an attacking profile that compares favourably with the division’s strongest sides.

    There is still a considerable amount of football to be played, and maintaining their current standards over an entire campaign will be the real challenge.

    In a recent development, however, the numbers provide plenty of encouragement for supporters in the capital. With consistent chance creation, contributions from across the squad and an increasingly convincing attacking record, Hertha have established themselves as genuine contenders for promotion.

    Their position at the top of 2. Bundesliga is no longer simply a reflection of a good run of results. The underlying statistics suggest there are solid reasons to believe their resurgence can continue.

    Hamburg’s next test is a trip to third-placed Eintracht Frankfurt, who have 17 points, on Saturday 21 November. Mainz host Nürnberg, the side directly above them, on Sunday 22 November.

    Palmer and Rogers show promise of star double act for Chelsea

    📅 25 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 27 min read (5490 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The stirring of what might yet be a great partnership between Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, although it will need to be, given some of the chaos that endures at Chelsea.

    This was a Premier League game played at a furious pace, and the two former Real Madrid team-mates in charge of the sides will not have seen much of the control all coaches seek. Xabi Alonso’s team eventually won with a goal from each of his attacking triumvirate of Rogers, Palmer and João Pedro – and at times it will have been painful for the newly introduced Chelsea manager.

    In a recent development, that was chiefly the fault of Robert Sánchez, who was embraced afterwards by Alonso, having demonstrated just how damaging a shaky goalkeeper can be to any serious team. Álvaro Arbeloa’s Fulham had their moments – and the best ones were granted to them by Sánchez. At a club that is such a restless trader of footballers, it feels remarkable that Sánchez has endured for so long.

    According to recent reports, alonso played down the significance of Sánchez’s errors, although he cannot seriously be considering sticking to his mantra of “relax and carry on”. That was, he noted, his response to the first-half Sánchez mistake that let in Josh King’s shot for Fulham’s first goal. Sánchez could have done a lot better with Gonzalo García’s goal after the break.

    Fulham have equalised against Chelsea thanks to Josh King's low strike 💥 pic.twitter.com/WCLKB7XqeE.

    Gonzalo Garcia has scored on his Premier League debut after Robert Sanchez spilled Castagne's shot 🤯 pic.twitter.com/BmP6eqwkuN.

    In a recent development, chelsea have a lot of faith that Mike Penders, the 21-year-old Belgian on the bench for this game, will be their first-choice goalkeeper eventually. The situation seems rather more urgent and with Penders likely to feature against Luton Town on Thursday night in the Carabao Cup it would appear a massive decision is looming for Alonso.

    Recent findings suggest that in terms of the Palmer-Rogers axis, this was very promising, although there was no doubting the senior figure in this. Palmer’s ball set João Pedro free in the first minute, the Brazilian lifting a well-judged nudge over Bernd Leno.

    "A flying start under Xabi Alonso!" Chelsea lead against Fulham after just 31 seconds 🤯 pic.twitter.com/LrkYxOReFB.

    It was Palmer who was crucial to the second for Rogers, made by Maxence Lacroix on his debut. Palmer stroked in the third on 49 minutes with the easy confidence of a man in form.

    It has been revealed that A goal for Morgan Rogers on his Chelsea debut! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/hphe8y077v.

    It has been revealed that "Cole Palmer back to his best!"Palmer has scored to double Chelsea's lead! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/zo6e0Vdcgq.

    “I am very happy for Cole,” Alonso stated. “I have really enjoyed seeing him play with the dynamism and the freedom and the responsibility... when Cole feels this way we have a better team and a better Cole.”.

    Palmer makes it look very easy in this form, capable of switching the direction of play a beat before anyone else spots the opportunity. He and his old Manchester City academy friend Rogers came off before the end, Palmer having demonstrated some discomfort chasing a ball. Asked afterwards how ready he felt, Palmer responded in kind. “Did you not watch the game? I’m only joking, I’m ready... it was a difficult season with injuries and whatnot, but through the summer and since I’ve been back I’ve worked extra hard.”.

    If there was an attacker to compare with him on the other side it was King, who looks even better. The 19-year-old was way ahead of Arbeloa’s two young Real Madrid imports. García toiled away and took his chance, but César Palacios struggled for any impact in a position tucked in on the left. Oscar Bobb and King gave Fulham some edge but the concern, as ever, will be where Fulham get their goals.

    Arbeloa pushed his full-backs high and encouraged Sander Berge to drop deep to get on the ball in the first passing phase. The Norwegian delayed too long in challenging João Pedro for Chelsea’s third – backing off and allowing Palmer to overlap to receive the pass.

    Sánchez had not been the only concern for Chelsea. Back in the team, Levi Colwill misjudged a challenge on King in the first half and was relieved that the card was only yellow. Roméo Lavia took a wild swing at Calvin Bassey and was also booked. Moisés Caicedo was not fit to play. Enzo Fernández was on the bench and would come on in the second half to the kind of reception from opposition fans to which he will quickly become familiar.

    There was a grin from the Argentine at those who berated him from the home stands when he returned at half-time. Fernández worked hard to transmit a general sense that the abuse did not land, although he will be relieved that the Chelsea fans were supportive. His future still feels very much in play.

    It has been revealed that it was Palmer’s subtle ball through that gave João Pedro the chance with 32 seconds of the game played. The ball came forward immediately from Lacroix’s firm header from defence. The Frenchman delivered a very accomplished assist for Rogers’s first-half goal. Before that King had equalised. There was an exchange with Timothy Castagne, and King looked up just inside the box and decided to have a swing at it. Sánchez was close enough to grasp the ball and somehow failed to do so.

    Sánchez would later push a Castagne shot in the direction of García, who stooped and nodded the ball over the goalkeeper after Palmer had scored Chelsea’s third. This second error was unfortunate, but it is the kind of thing that happens to a goalkeeper as erratic as the one for whom Chelsea’s hierarchy seem to have such patience.

    It has been revealed that “We concede goals in the first minute, the end of the first half and the beginning of the second half and there are not worse moments to concede. But we demonstrated character and personality and I am very proud of how my players responded. We deserved a little bit more but football is not about what you deserve, it is about what you take. If you lose against a team like Chelsea they [should] have to do a little bit more. For me, they are easy goals for them and mistakes we cannot make. We need to improve and be more ready in the first minute, that is for sure.

    In a recent development, “We are on our way and we will keep improving. The first thing I want to see is a competitive team. We were tonight, we tried our best and tried to play our football against a team like Chelsea, which is not easy. I believe in them and I believe in young players. I think they have the energy and ambition I want and they fit in the way I play. Josh King is absolutely amazing. I am really happy with him. Gonzalo [Garcia] scored and Cesar [Palacios] did well. I think they need a bit more time but they are doing great and making an impact already.”.

    "We need to help them, not to rely everything on them" Xabi Alonso speaking about Chelsea's 'special' front three 🔵 pic.twitter.com/JnSBoNexF4.

    "Arsenal DON'T win the league if they have Ramsdale and not Raya" 🧤@Carra23 and @GNev2 think that upgrading the goalkeeper position could be the 'last piece' for Chelsea 🧩 pic.twitter.com/UBzMCFmxpp.

    "You can see in his eyes, he's ready to prove people wrong""Best player on the pitch by a mile" 👏Morgan Rogers reacts to his debut and the performance of Cole Palmer pic.twitter.com/M7JKk1MQ8U.

    Recent findings suggest that "How ready are you?""Did you not watch the game?" 😅Cole Palmer says he is 'hungry' and ready to get back to his best! pic.twitter.com/xpg5zJl9k0.

    2 - Cole Palmer tonight vs Fulham:1 goal1 assist5 dribbles completed5 shots3 chances created7 ball recoveries10 duels wonHe was only the second player on record since 2006-07 to record all of these numbers in a Premier League game.Cold. pic.twitter.com/uW4YPeHNnD.

    “There were things to really like. On paper, that front three [for Chelsea] is sensational. It really is. It looked it in the game. I think Joao Pedro is fantastic. [Morgan] Rogers’ first game, what a start. But when you think of him, [Cole] Palmer and Pedro; that is as good as anything in the Premier League right now.

    “But I do think concerns defensively. They conceded a couple of goals and you look at the goalkeeper. They have to sort the goalkeeper problem out because it is going to come back to haunt them this season, as it did tonight.”.

    August 27: Fulham vs AFC Wimbledon (League Cup)August 30: Sunderland vs Fulham (Premier League)September 5: Fulham vs Crystal Palace (Premier League)September 12: Liverpool vs Fulham (Premier League)September 20: Fulham vs Manchester United (Premier League).

    “The attacking play, Cole Palmer was sensational. If you talk about Cole Palmer getting back to his best you have got a £120m-£125m player there. [Morgan] Rogers getting a goal. Those two being electric with Joao Pedro up front. The front three were brilliant tonight. One of the best things I have seen this weekend.

    “They have added an experience player at centre-back, centre midfield and centre forward. I do not know if Emi Martinez is available or not but someone like that needs to come in at Chelsea, because that will undermine everything they do. The positives for Fulham came from the encouragement [Robert] Sanchez gave them with the goals. The goals were both mistakes. It is a problem.”.

    The final whistle is blown at Craven Cottage and Chelsea hold on to win 3-2 to give Xabi Alonso a win in his first game in charge. Alvaro Arbeloa’s first game as Fulham boss ends in defeat. An absorbing west London derby.

    Garcia throws himself to the ground as Sessegnon sends in a cross but that is never going to be a penalty.

    Will there be one more chance for Fulham to try and find an equaliser? Time is running out for the hosts.

    Sources indicate that pedro has the ball in the back of the Fulham net but Quenda was offside in the build-up. A quick VAR check proves so.

    There will be four added minutes.

    Surely there is another goal in this one? It is a surprise there has not been since Garcia got a goal back for Fulham.

    The latest booking of the game goes the way of Castagne, who cynically trips Colwill.

    According to recent reports, sessegnon is played in down the left channel and flicks it past Acheampong inside the Chelsea penalty area. Sessegnon gets his shot away from a narrow angle and it is straight at Sanchez.

    Recent findings suggest that palmer looks like he might have cramp in his calf and is going to be replaced by Estevao. Quenda also comes on for Chelsea, coming on for Rogers.

    Fulham make an attacking alteration as Muniz replaces Robinson.

    Recent findings suggest that that is a huge, huge chance for Fulham to equalise. Robinson is played in behind the Chelsea defence with a long ball in behind and Sanchez is in no-man’s land out of his goal. Robinson just has to lift it over Sanchez from the edge of the box but his effort goes wide. Fulham should be on level terms.

    Recent findings suggest that fulham fans think they are about to be awarded a free-kick right outside the box but instead the free-kick goes the other way. It was a clear dive from Bassey, who is rightly booked for simulation.

    James is the third Chelsea player into the book for cynically pulling King back. James then has the cheek to wag his finger at King, as if it was not a foul, yet it was a clear booking. James had to be careful there as some referees may not have taken too kindly to that.

    Double change for Fulham as Kevin and Sessegnon are brought on.

    That would have been a great goal from King. He has already scored once and is inches away from his second. He receives a pass on the turn from Robinson and drives towards the Chelsea box. He then cuts inside onto his right, beating Lacroix with ease, and nearly beats Sanchez at his near post but his shot goes inches wide.

    Sources indicate that this is a very open, end-to-end game and you would fully expect more goals in this one. I would be very surprised if this one ended 3-2. Both defences are looking leaky.

    Fulham are going to make their substitution of the night as Charles comes on for his debut having signed from Southampton, replacing Bobb.

    Enzo is being booed a lot by the home fans every time he touches the ball.

    It has been revealed that chelsea are the first to turn to their bench. Enzo is coming on and is met by a lot of boos, mostly though from the home fans as the majority of the travelling Chelsea fans are applauding him. Chavarria is also on to make his Chelsea debut. Hato and Lavia head off.

    There is a new rule being implemented. Hato takes far too long over a throw-in and Fulham are therefore awarded the throw-in instead.

    It has been revealed that when Palmer put Chelsea 3-1 up, the visitors looked in control of this match. Fast forward five minutes and the momentum has completely switched around. What an absorbing opening Monday night of the season!

    The Fulham debutant gives them life and this game is not over. Castagne is found making a run in behind and cuts back inside onto his left inside the Chelsea penalty area. His shot is straight at Sanchez, who can only parry it straight into the path of Garcia, who heads into the ground and the ball bounces over Sanchez into the Chelsea net. Another poor piece of goalkeeping from Sanchez.

    Gonzalo Garcia has scored on his Premier League debut after Robert Sanchez spilled Castagne's shot 🤯 pic.twitter.com/BmP6eqwkuN.

    All members of Chelsea’s starting front three have got on the scoresheet tonight and Palmer also has an assist to his name.

    Chelsea come close to a fourth as Hato squares it for Rogers inside the Fulham box but Robinson nips in just in front to clear.

    Recent findings suggest that he came close to scoring moments ago and now he does get on the scoresheet. Pedro gets onto the end of a flicked-on header by Rogers near halfway and drives into the Fulham half. As he gets to the Fulham penalty area, he waits for the overlapping run of Palmer and times the pass just right. Palmer, from a narrow angle, puts it between Leno’s legs and into the far corner.

    "Cole Palmer back to his best!"Palmer has scored to double Chelsea's lead! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/zo6e0Vdcgq.

    Sources indicate that palmer does brilliantly down Chelsea’s right to skip past a number of defenders and moves into the Fulham penalty area. He opens up his body and curls one towards the far corner. He is adamant that there is a deflection but a goal kick is given. Replays show Palmer may have had a point.

    We are back under way at Craven Cottage.

    Nottingham Forest are ramping up their pursuit of Chelsea’s Liam Delap as Oliver Glasner eyes two major signings before the window closes.

    Forest are in talks with Chelsea over a potential loan deal for the forward after he was made available at Stamford Bridge and not included in their opening-day squad against Fulham.

    Negotiations are ongoing, but Delap fits the profile of striker Forest are prioritising and is a long-term target for both the club and Glasner from his spell at Crystal Palace.

    Possession: Fulham 60%-40% ChelseaShots: 7-13Shots on target: 2-5Corners: 4-3Touches in opposition box: 16-18.

    An absorbing first half at Craven Cottage is brought to a close and Chelsea take a 2-1 lead into the break. Pedro put them ahead inside the first minute before King equalised for Fulham. However Rogers, on his Chelsea debut, put the visitors back in front not long before half-time.

    There will be two added minutes at the end of this first half.

    Palmer, who has run the show for Chelsea in this first half, is inches away from putting the visitors 3-1 up. Both sides have been guilty of giving the ball away in dangerous areas and Fulham do so on this occasion. Palmer then curls an effort from the edge of the box but his shot goes just wide of the far post.

    Sources indicate that the British record transfer puts Chelsea back in front on his official debut. It stems from great play from centre-back Lacroix, who finds himself in an advanced position and receives a pass from Palmer on the right side of the box. Lacroix cuts it across to Rogers, who makes no mistake from 12 yards out. Assist and goal both coming from fresh signings.

    It has been revealed that A goal for Morgan Rogers on his Chelsea debut! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/hphe8y077v.

    Fulham fail to clear a cross from James into their box and Hato’s header falls at the feet of Lavia, whose shot from close range is saved by Leno.

    Is Colwill lucky to still be on the pitch? The ball is played in behind the Chelsea defence and Colwill appeared to throw his arm across King but no foul is given. That could so easily have been given as a free-kick and a second yellow card.

    It has been revealed that rogers drives towards the Fulham box and cuts inside onto his right foot. His effort is blocked by Cuenca before James’ first-time shot is straight at Leno.

    In a recent development, chelsea are inches from going back in front. It stems from great work from Palmer, who drives down Chelsea’s right. His cross from the right side of the box picks out Pedro near the penalty spot. The Brazilian volleys it first time but his effort goes just wide.

    Sources indicate that fulham are on top at the moment and Chelsea are lucky shaky as they are under the cosh inside their own box. King is playing really well, finding pockets of space down Fulham’s right and looking a real threat.

    According to recent reports, fulham are back on level terms but it is really poor goalkeeping from Sanchez. King, who had just threatened down Fulham’s right, receives a pass from Castagne on the right touchline and takes a touch into the Chelsea box. King then fires his shot away at the near post and gets plenty of power on it but there is no way Sanchez should be beaten. He is beaten and Fulham equalise. Good strike from King but terrible keeping from Sanchez.

    Fulham have equalised against Chelsea thanks to Josh King's low strike 💥 pic.twitter.com/WCLKB7XqeE.

    Sources indicate that chelsea haven’t spent all that money on Rogers for his defending, but Alonso won’t have liked the way he let Josh King to run past him to collect the ball and smash Fulham level. Rogers switched off there.

    King does brilliantly to drive down Fulham’s right and flashes a dangerous ball across the six-yard box but none of his teammates are on hand to meet the cross.

    Fulham are flirting with danger in and around their box and are a touch fortunate not to concede a second goal.

    Sources indicate that down the other end, King is urged to shoot from outside the box and he obliges. It looks like it should be a fairly routine save for Sanchez but the Chelsea keeper looks uncomfortable and pushes it behind for a corner. The delivery comes to the near post and King, who lays it off the edge of the box. It comes to Palacios, who cannot guide his effort on target.

    Industry observers note that chelsea started this game well but have lost control and are asking for trouble. The latest example sees Sanchez take too long to clear and he accidentally allows the ball to go out before clearing to gift Fulham a corner. Bobb’s delivery is headed away at the near post by James.

    That is strong one-vs-one defending from Bassey. Palmer lifts the ball over the top to pick out the run of Pedro, who is dispossessed inside the Fulham box by Bassey.

    In a recent development, moments later, Lavia flies into a reckless challenge on Bassey and is booked. Lavia looks stunned at that decision but he is perhaps on the fortunate side that VAR did not advise the referee to have a further look at that on the screen. Lavia was out of control and could have easily been in more trouble. Two Chelsea players already into the book and were a little bit lucky.

    Palmer had just one Premier League assist to his name throughout last season and has already matched that tally tonight on the opening weekend.

    In a recent development, colwill is in trouble. Could Chelsea go down to 10 men early? He loses possession poorly inside his own half and then resorts to hacking Bobb down with a nasty challenge. Was Colwill the last man and could Bobb have gone racing in on goal? Colwill is booked and is perhaps a touch fortunate, although what saved him is that you perhaps could not definitively say that it was a denial of a goal-scoring opportunity.

    How do Alvaro Arbeloa and his Fulham side react now they are a goal down early?

    Recent findings suggest that with their first attack of the Xabi Alonso era, Chelsea hit the front inside the opening minute of this west London derby. Lacroix’s header from halfway finds Palmer, who plays it into the path of Pedro. The Brazilian, fresh from signing a fresh deal at the club, takes it in his stride and, from inside the Fulham penalty area, lifts it over Leno and into the far corner. A fine finish from Pedro and Alonso has the perfect start.

    "A flying start under Xabi Alonso!" Chelsea lead against Fulham after just 31 seconds 🤯 pic.twitter.com/LrkYxOReFB.

    According to recent reports, could Joao Pedro be the man to finally lift the curse of the number nine shirt at Chelsea? Liam Delap tried and failed last season. Pedro has taken it this term and has started like a train with that early goal. Pedro has also been prolific in pre-season and has been widely tipped to be one of the Premier League’s top scorers.

    Before we get going, we take a moment to remember the great Kevin Keegan, who managed Fulham in the late 1990s.

    We are under way at Craven Cottage in the final game on this opening weekend of the latest Premier League season.

    Alvaro Arbeloa is out on the pitch for the first time in the Premier League. A friendly if not rapturous welcome from the home fans. He’s rolled his sleeves up and he’s ready to go - literally, his skinny fit jacket has sleeves rolled up tight. It looks quite uncomfortable.

    It might be a new season and a new manager, but Chelsea are still doing their pre-match huddle. Fortunately, it was nowhere near the referee or the centre circle. It seemed to be captain Reece James doing all the talking.

    It has been revealed that both sides emerge from the tunnel at Craven Cottage and we are moments away from kick-off in this west London derby. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up tonight:.

    The boos for Fernandez from the Fulham fans got a lot louder when the players stepped on the pitch. Some people chanted something rather nasty beginning with ‘w’ as well.

    There were a few boos from the Fulham fans when Enzo Fernandez’s name was read out ahead of kick-off. Clearly the England fans at Craven Cottage haven’t forgotten what happened against Argentina. Fernandez was booed by some Chelsea supporters in pre-season, but there were no loud jeers from the away end during the team announcements.

    According to recent reports, “During the week they had a few setbacks. With Moises [Caicedo], and with any [player], we do not want to take too much risk. They were not ready to play tonight. We need to go week-by-week but for tonight they were not ready.”.

    According to recent reports, chelsea certainly have an army of staff. I just counted 13 staff members helping the players through their warm-up. One of them is the new set-piece coach Austin MacPhee, who is carrying around a clipboard, presumably with all his set-piece tricks on it. Culture guru Willi Isa is also out there, as is former interim manager Calum McFarlane.

    Chelsea’s £117m man Morgan Rogers has just run out for his warm up ahead of his competitive debut for the club. He’s kept in close contact with his best mate Cole Palmer, going through a few passing drills and doing a few keepy-ups. He looks relaxed so far.

    Recent findings suggest that the most interesting piece of Chelsea team news is that there is no Enzo Fernandez in the starting line-up, despite the surprise absence of Moises Caicedo. Instead, Romeo Lavia will partner Reece James in the centre of midfield, with Caicedo presumably injured. There is still an expectation that Manchester City will bid for Fernandez before the transfer window shuts, but the Argentine is on the substitutes’ bench. As expected, there is no place in the Chelsea squad for Nico Jackson and Liam Delap, both of whom have not travelled and are expected to leave Stamford Bridge. Aston Villa remain favourites to land Jackson, although Atletico Madrid have been showing an interest. Nottingham Forest are leading the race for Delap.

    Morgan Rogers and Maxence Lacroix make their full Chelsea debuts this evening. Fellow fresh signings Danny Welbeck, Valentin Barco, Pep Chavarria and Geovany Quenda are on the bench, as is Enzo Fernandez, who has been linked with a move away. Moises Caicedo is not in the matchday squad.

    Chelsea: Sanchez; Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill; Gusto, Lavia, James, Hato; Palmer, Pedro, Rogers.Substitutes: Penders, Chavarria, Barco, Enzo, Neto, Gittens, Estevao, Welbeck, Quenda.

    According to recent reports, no more excuses. No more jam tomorrow. It is time for Chelsea to fight for the Premier League title this season. Anything else should be deemed a disappointment.

    This is Chelsea version 3.0 under BlueCo, who bought the club four years ago. First there was Todd Boehly’s trolley dash, then came Behdad Eghbali’s youth club. This summer the focus has been on being Premier League-ready.

    In a recent development, off the pitch, the timing might be right for Boehly to be discussing the sale of his shares to Eghbali’s Clearlake Capital. But on it, Chelsea look better equipped to re-enter the title conversation than at any point in the BlueCo era.

    Sunday:Manchester City 2 Bournemouth 1Brighton 4 Aston Villa 0Newcastle 2 Liverpool 2.

    Let's get it.#CFC | #FULCHE pic.twitter.com/G2M8LknNgV.

    In a recent development, monday Night Fulham. ⚪️ pic.twitter.com/Oxuni9yiez.

    Industry observers note that two former Liverpool, Real Madrid and Spain teammates go head-to-head in the dugouts at Craven Cottage as Fulham host Chelsea in a west London derby to round out the opening weekend of the fresh Premier League season. Alvaro Arbeloa and Xabi Alonso were teammates at Liverpool, Real Madrid and Spain and both had stints as Real Madrid manager last season but have new homes in London. Arbeloa has replaced Marco Silva, who is now at Benfica, whilst Alonso is Liam Rosenior’s permanent replacement. This is the first time a manager’s Premier League debut has come against someone he also played alongside in the competition.

    “I know Alonso well because I have watched so many games of his teams,” Arbeloa said. “We have to be ready, and if we want to beat them we will have to play very well. I spoke to Xabi a few days ago. But not about football; both of our families are coming to London, and we are very good friends, until Monday night [tonight]. We will be there on the touchline, so close for 90 minutes, and we will give everything for our clubs. For those 90 minutes, we are not friends.”.

    In a recent development, arbeloa has gone back to his former club to add a couple of players in the shape of Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios. The opening weekend has not served Fulham well of late; they have won just one of their last six Premier League opening weekend fixtures. They concluded their pre-season with a 1-0 win over Stuttgart.

    Sources indicate that chelsea have been very active in the transfer market this summer, breaking the British transfer record to sign Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa as well as adding experience through the likes of Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck, whilst the likes of Marc Cucurella, Andrey Santos and Trevoh Chalobah have moved on. They finished off their pre-season with a 3-1 victory over Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge just over a week ago.

    “We feel ready,” Alonso remarked. “We have prepared the whole pre-season with some players from the first day, other ones coming later, but the desire, the ambition, the hunger to start the Premier League is already in the building each training [session] and we are looking forward to it.”.

    Enzo Fernandez has been strongly linked with a move away this summer, with Manchester City’s interest well-known.

    “Enzo is a Chelsea player,” Alonso added. “He is a top, top player. He is training really well since he started 10 days ago with the team, very integrated. We are happy with him and he is getting ready for Monday. He is training really well, good attitude and that is what we want. He is trying his best to prepare for the kick-off of the Premier League.”.

    Recent findings suggest that these sides finished on the same number of points (52) last season, with Chelsea finishing ahead on goal difference. It was one win apiece for each club in the two Premier League meetings last season. Nearly a year ago, Chelsea won 2-0 at Stamford Bridge whilst Fulham won 2-1 in this fixture at Craven Cottage back in January. Chelsea have won six of the past eight Premier League meetings at Craven Cottage.

    • In a recent development, bayer Leverkusen beat Stuttgart 3-2 in the Frauen Bundesliga on Monday 16 November, with Caroline Victoria Kehrer scoring the winner in the second minute of stoppage time.
    • In a recent development, leverkusen led at the break.
    • Stuttgart answered immediately after the restart.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, bayer Leverkusen beat Stuttgart 3-2 in the Frauen Bundesliga on Monday 16 November, with Caroline Victoria Kehrer scoring the winner in the second minute of stoppage time. Stuttgart had just drawn level through Mira Arouna in the 87th minute. Julia Boike refereed the matchday 10 fixture.

    In a recent development, leverkusen led at the break. Loreen Bender opened the scoring in the 20th minute, set up by Cornelia Kramer, and the visitors took a 1-0 lead into half-time.

    Stuttgart answered immediately after the restart. Dafina Redzepi equalised in the 46th minute, and the Stuttgart forward went on to have the biggest influence on the match. She was rated 8.86, the highest on the pitch, with a goal, an assist, 3 shots and 5 key passes across the full 90 minutes.

    Leverkusen restored their advantage in the 59th minute when Maja Sternad finished from a Valentina Mädl pass. Sternad was booked 3 minutes later, after Luzie Zähringer had been cautioned for Stuttgart in the 54th minute. Those were the only cards of the night.

    Industry observers note that redzepi then turned provider, laying on the 87th-minute equaliser for Arouna, who scored with her only shot in 21 minutes on the pitch. The draw lasted barely 5 minutes. Mädl delivered again, and Kehrer converted in the second minute of stoppage time, having been on the field for just 2 minutes. Mädl finished with 2 assists in a 33-minute appearance.

    The numbers favoured the winners without being one-sided. Leverkusen had 54% of the ball, completed 366 of 483 passes against Stuttgart’s 266 of 387, and put 8 shots on target. Stuttgart goalkeeper L. Giuliani’s side were kept in the game by 6 saves. Stuttgart actually shot more often, 15 times to 13, but only 4 of those efforts tested the Leverkusen goal and 8 went wide. Expected goals finished 1.43 to 1.2 in Leverkusen’s favour.

    Recent findings suggest that leverkusen were caught offside 4 times. Stuttgart were not flagged once.

    ⏹️ Ist das bitter! Wir unterliegen nach starkem Fight knapp mit 2:3 gegen die Werkself. Die zwischenzeitlichen Ausgleiche zunächst durch Dafina Redzepi und anschließend durch Mira Arouna reichen nicht für den Punktgewinn. Köpfe hoch, Mädels!

    VfB Stuttgart 🆚 Bayer 04 Leverkusen 2:3 #VfBFrauen | #VfB.

    — VfB Stuttgart News (@vfb-stuttgart.bsky.social) 2026-11-16T18:54:42.437Z.

    The win leaves Leverkusen fifth on 19 points, level with Werder Bremen in fourth and separated only by goal difference, 4 against 6. Eintracht Frankfurt are third on 20 points. Bayern Munich lead on 30 points from 10 games, with VfL Wolfsburg second on 24.

    It is a second straight league win for Leverkusen after a 2-0 victory over Hamburger SV. Kramer, provider for the opener, has 6 league goals this season, 2 behind leading scorer E. Peddemors of VfL Wolfsburg.

    According to recent reports, for Stuttgart, the defeat ended a two-match winning run that had brought a 3-0 win over SGS Essen and a 3-1 victory against Mainz 05. Before that, they had lost three in a row, conceding 12 goals against Union Berlin, Bayern Munich and Eintracht Frankfurt. They are ninth with 11 points and a goal difference of -11.

    Leverkusen travel to Union Berlin on Friday 20 November. Stuttgart visit SC Freiburg two days later, on Sunday 22 November.

    Industry News: Paul Scholes calls Man United's bizarre lap of honour 'embarrassing' after Gary Neville claimed stars are risking 'emotional damage' with post-match ritual

    📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (937 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By TARA ANSON-WALSH, FOOTBALL REPORTER and LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.
    • Published: 04:05 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 11:18 EST, 11 November 2026.
    • Paul Scholes has branded Manchester United's post-match walks of honour 'embarrassing' after Gary Neville suggested the squad are causing themselves 'emotional damage'.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By TARA ANSON-WALSH, FOOTBALL REPORTER and LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

    Published: 04:05 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 11:18 EST, 11 November 2026.

    Paul Scholes has branded Manchester United's post-match walks of honour 'embarrassing' after Gary Neville suggested the squad are causing themselves 'emotional damage'.

    United staged another incredible fightback to snatch a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at Old Trafford after trailing by two goals heading into injury-time.

    But it wasn't enough to spare the club from the humiliation of being in the relegation zone for the next two weeks – the longest United have spent there since 1986.

    After the full-time whistle, the United players conducted a post-match walk of honour as the fans chanted Michael Carrick's name in a defiant show of support for their beleaguered boss – a move a number of ex-United stars have called into question.

    'I tell you one thing they have to do, is stop these laps of honour after the game,' Scholes said, speaking on The Good, The Bad & The Football, sponsored by Midnite. 'What the f***?'.

    Nicky Butt added: 'It's p***ing me off,' before Scholes continued: 'They are so bad. Not so much Michael, the team as well. It's embarrassing. It should be after the last game of the season. I feel sorry for them.'.

    Paul Scholes has torn into Manchester United for their regular post-match laps of honour (Source: YouTube/The Good, The Bad and The Football).

    Gary Neville, meanwhile, remarked the habit has become 'painful to watch' as a United fan.

    Neville, meanwhile, remarked on NBC Sports: 'You have got to admire their persistence, they kept going. 'Defensive errors were shocking and we'll discuss that shortly. But this lap around the pitch...

    It has been revealed that 'I played for Manchester United 602 times and I always appreciated the fans at the end of the game, but this pattern of them walking around the pitch after defeats by Bournemouth and a 4-4 at home against Aston Villa, it's almost painful to watch. They're almost causing themselves emotional damage.

    In a recent development, 'This just can't go on, can it? It's absolutely desperate. Michael will be proud of them and the fans are singing his name because they love him but this is a really sorry situation.'.

    Carrick was involved in a spiky back-and-forth with Sky Sports' Patrick Davison when it was suggested to him that he could step down:.

    Davison: 'What do you expect to happen over the next few weeks? If you thought walking away was the best thing, you'd probably do it.'.

    Carrick: 'It's not going to happen, no.'.

    Davison: 'What do you expect to happen? Clearly there's going to be conversation?'.

    Davison: 'You would assume so, right?'.

    Davison: 'What do you think, Michael?'.

    Carrick: 'You're telling me what you think, aren't you?'.

    Sources indicate that davison: 'I'm asking you what you think? What do you expect to happen?'.

    Sources indicate that carrick: 'We understand the situation; we haven't won enough games. But I expect to move forward and keep working on things we've been working on, showing a lot of the good in the game today, tighten up on a few mistakes and win football matches.'.

    He added: 'Michael will be proud of them and the fans are singing his name because they love him but this is a really sorry situation' (Source: YouTube/NBC Sports).

    Carrick insisted 'it's not going to happen' when it was put to him that he could walk away if he thought that would be the 'best thing' for the club.

    Then, speaking in his post-match press conference, Carrick expressed confidence his side could still turn things around this season.

    Sources indicate that 'One hundred per cent,' he said. 'I think there's more than enough. Goals change games and we've got to deal with it and it's something we have to improve on drastically. But there's more than enough, we're just making it too difficult for ourselves at the moment in certain times….

    In a recent development, 'I'm quite clear with what direction the club needs to go in. We've just got to win games.'.

    Amid a wave of fan protests expressing their discontent towards INEOS and the Glazer family on Sunday, Neville has suggested that the club's hierarchy 'don't have a clue what to do' on Carrick.

    Recent findings suggest that he added: 'You can keep changing the manager and thinking that's going to be the answer. But this has been proven now over eight managers in 12 years - that's not the answer.

    According to recent reports, 'Michael could leave, Michael might stay, we don't know. The ownership don't have a clue what to do.

    Recent findings suggest that 'It's rinse and repeat. (Ruben) Amorim, (Erik) Ten Hag, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Carrick, Jose Mourinho, Louis van Gaal, David Moyes, Ralf Rangnick - some of them are world-class managers who have had success; there are a lot of promising young managers there, ex-players who know the club as well.

    'None of it has worked because if you recruit badly, if you've got a poor performance department, a poor recruitment department, you've not got leadership that is strong right through the spine of the football club, you will fail.

    'Every organisation in the world will fail if you've not got an aligned leadership from top to bottom - your board and your ownership right the way through to the person who is stood on the pitch trying to play football.

    'There are real concerns within that football club; you've got people doing those jobs who have never done those jobs before in senior positions.'.

    Following Germany's 3-1 victory over Serbia on Friday, Jürgen Klopp is planning to make two changes to his side for Monday's final 2026/27 UEFA Nations League Group A2 fixture against the Netherlands.

    According to Bild, Nico Schlotterbeck and Nathaniel Brown will be drafted into the starting line-up in defence, just as Bulinews predicted in our match preview.

    Brown is in line to come in at left-back at the expense of Maximilian Mittelstädt, while Schlotterbeck will partner Jonathan Tah in central defence, with Malick Thiaw dropping to the bench.

    Klopp's side can secure their place in the UEFA Nations League quarter-finals with a victory in Berlin on Monday.

    • Manchester United hope Marcus Rashford can be fit for their next game at Liverpool a week on Sunday after the England star began a new treatment programme.
    • Rashford returned to Old Trafford in the summer after a year on loan at Barcelona having sustained a hip injury at the World Cup.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

    Published: 12:00 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 12:00 EST, 11 November 2026.

    Manchester United hope Marcus Rashford can be fit for their next game at Liverpool a week on Sunday after the England star began a new treatment programme.

    Rashford returned to Old Trafford in the summer after a year on loan at Barcelona having sustained a hip injury at the World Cup.

    The 29-year-old played in the first six league games of the season – as well as the Carabao Cup tie against Brighton and, most recently, the Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid in mid-October – but aggravated the problem which has spread to his groin.

    Rashford visited a groin specialist in Dublin last week with a member of United’s medical staff and a upcoming recovery programme has now been put in place.

    Rashford is said to have a good relationship with Michael Carrick and wanted to give the head coach his support.

    But playing while carrying the injury only made it worse. It’s understood that he even offered to go on the bench at Chelsea recently but the club decided against it.

    Man United star Marcus Rashford is seen in a TikTok posted by his hairdresser on Tuesday.

    Rashford is hoping to be back and available for the game against Liverpool.

    However, Rashford will continue to work his way back to fitness during the international break and United hope he will be available for the trip to Anfield to face Liverpool.

    With Carrick expected to be sacked and replaced by Mauricio Pochettino, it could well be the Argentine’s first game in charge on his return to the Premier League having previously managed Tottenham, Chelsea and Southampton.

    Rashford has an impressive record against Liverpool with seven goals in 20 appearances against United’s biggest rivals.

    CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

    In a recent development, con la maglia della Lazio, Pancaro ha conquistato, tra gli altri trofei, lo storico scudetto del 2000. Durante l’incontro è tornato sui momenti più significativi della sua carriera nella Capitale e sul rapporto che conserva con il mondo laziale.

    #15380. Latest Update: Glasner made to wait for first win as Trafford thwarts Forest

    📅 25 Aug 2026 • ⏱️ 21m • 📚 Deep Dive (4165 w)
    📖 Baca
